sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: How should you handle your approach when you spot unusually slow traffic ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: When approaching unusually slow traffic, leave time to slow down or change lanes without sudden braking.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: What speed change should you anticipate behind a heavy truck or weak car climbing a long hill?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Expect a truck or an underpowered vehicle to lose speed on a long or steep hill.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: What top speed and rear marker apply to farm tractors, horse buggies, and road graders?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: The guide says farm tractors, animal-drawn vehicles, and road-maintenance vehicles generally move at twenty-five miles per hour or less and should display a rear slow-vehicle emblem.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: Why must you drop speed through shopping districts, parking lots, and downtown blocks?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: Reduce speed in busy shopping areas, parking lots, and downtown streets where vehicles start, stop, or move in different directions.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: Which four pinched or congested road features demand a drop in speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Slow for heavy rush-hour traffic, narrow bridges, tunnels, and toll-booth areas that limit maneuvering space.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: How must you adjust near schools, playgrounds, and neighborhood streets?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: Near schools, playgrounds, and residential streets, reduce speed and watch for children entering the roadway.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: Which two surprise hazards make weaving past car after car risky?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: When you repeatedly pass slower vehicles, those vehicles can unexpectedly change lanes and opposing traffic can suddenly appear on a two-lane road.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: What extra challenge hits heavy or slow vehicles pulling into traffic on an uphill grade?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Slow vehicles may need extra time to gain speed while entering traffic on a hill.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: How does the clear road distance visible ahead set your safe top speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: Choose a speed that lets you stop inside the clear distance you can see ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: What maximum speed does the guide set when rain or fog cuts forward sight to two hundred feet or less?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: When rain or fog restricts the view ahead to two hundred feet or less, the guide says not to exceed thirty miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: What must you do if blinding weather wipes out your view of the road ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: If you cannot see the roadway ahead, leave the road at a safe place and wait for the weather to improve.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: How should you adjust speed when nearing a hill crest or blind curve?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Near a hill or curve hiding the road ahead, adjust speed so you can stop for an unseen hazard.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: What sudden hazards require extra room beside a line of parked cars?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: Give parked vehicles extra space and be ready for someone opening a door or walking out from between them.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: How do you run the guide's four-second sight-distance check on the road?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: For the four-second sight-distance check, choose the farthest clearly visible fixed object and count until you reach it.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: What action is required if you pass your landmark before finishing the four-second sight count?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: If you reach the visible fixed object before four seconds have elapsed, reduce speed under the guide's sight-distance rule.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: Can an officer ticket you for driving too fast even when your speedometer matches the posted sign?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: A driver can be ticketed for excessive speed in the conditions even while driving at the posted limit.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: What crucial advantage do you gain by keeping more space behind the vehicle ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: More space between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead provides more time to respond to a hazard.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: How do you measure the guide's basic two-second following cushion behind a lead car?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: For the guide's two-second following check, count from when the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point until your vehicle reaches the same point.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: What should you do if your bumper reaches the marker before your two-second count finishes?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: If you reach the fixed point before finishing the two-second count, fall back and repeat the check.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: Why must you stretch your following distance whenever pavement turns wet, snowy, or icy?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Slippery roads require additional following space because stopping takes longer.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: How should you help a driver behind you who pulls out to overtake your vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: If a following driver wants to pass, ease speed to create room ahead for that driver to return to the lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: Why do motorcycles need extra following room on wet pavement, ice, loose gravel, or metal grates?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: Allow more following space behind motorcycles because wet, icy, gravel, or metal surfaces can make a rider fall.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: Why should you drop farther back behind trucks, buses, vans, or trailers?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: Fall farther back behind trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles towing trailers when their drivers may not be able to see you.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: How does pulling a trailer change your vehicle's stopping distance?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: Towing adds weight and increases the distance needed to stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: How must darkness, fog, or heavy rain change your following gap?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: Poor visibility calls for an increase in following distance.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: How should you manage space around police cruisers, ambulances, and fire engines?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: Give police vehicles, ambulances, and fire trucks room to carry out their work.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: Why must you keep extra space behind buses and hazmat tankers approaching train tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: Near a railroad crossing, leave space for buses or hazardous-material vehicles that must stop there.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: Why should you leave extra bumper gap when stopped behind someone on an uphill slope?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: When stopped on an incline, leave extra room because the vehicle ahead might roll backward as it starts.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: About how many total feet does the guide's example take to stop from forty miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: The guide illustrates total stopping distance as about one hundred twenty-four feet at forty miles per hour.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: About how many total feet does the guide's example require to stop from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: At fifty-five miles per hour, the guide's stopping-distance example is about two hundred twenty-five feet.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: Within what specific distance must you always be able to stop when driving at night?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: Night driving requires stopping within the distance illuminated by the headlights.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: What kind of driving conditions are posted speed-limit signs built around?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Posted speed limits assume ideal conditions, so rain, ice, poor visibility, or heavy traffic can require a lower speed.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: To how many seconds does the guide stretch its basic two-second following rule in tough conditions?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: The guide says some conditions require a four-second following interval rather than its basic two-second check.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: Which two habits help drivers behind you keep a safe cushion without surprises?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: Help following drivers by maintaining a steady speed and signaling before you slow or stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.front: Where should you pull over to pick up or drop off riders safely?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.expected_back: Choose a location away from moving traffic when picking up or dropping off passengers.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.front: How should you handle traffic behind you right before backing into a parallel parking spot?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.expected_back: Before parallel parking with following traffic, signal, pull beside the space, and let vehicles behind pass before starting the parking maneuver.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.front: How should you let faster vehicles pass when you are traveling slower than normal traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.expected_back: Use a safe turnout or roadside place to let others pass if you are traveling more slowly than surrounding traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.front: What two calm moves does the guide give for shedding a driver tailgating you?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.expected_back: For a tailgater, move into the right lane when possible; otherwise wait for a clear path ahead and gradually reduce speed so the following driver can pass.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.front: Why must you never slam or tap brakes sharply just to warn off a tailgater?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.expected_back: Do not brake abruptly to discourage a tailgater, because that raises the risk of being hit from behind.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.front: How should you position your car relative to vehicles in neighboring lanes on a multilane road?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.expected_back: Maintain side space instead of remaining beside another vehicle on a multilane road.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.front: Where inside your lane should you track instead of hugging the center line?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.expected_back: Keep your vehicle centered in its lane rather than crowding the opposing lane's center line.

sec12-card-sec12-F44.front: Why do parked cars along the curb deserve extra lateral clearance as you pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.expected_back: Give extra side clearance to parked vehicles where a door, pedestrian, or departing vehicle may enter your path.

sec12-card-sec12-F45.front: How should you steer when hazards box you in on both the left and right at once?
sec12-card-sec12-F45.expected_back: When hazards exist on both sides, steer between them and give more clearance to the side presenting the greater danger.

sec12-card-sec12-F46.front: What should you do when approaching a bicyclist ahead at the exact moment an oncoming car nears?
sec12-card-sec12-F46.expected_back: When passing a bicycle with an oncoming vehicle approaching, slow and let that vehicle go by before passing the bicycle.

sec12-card-sec12-F47.front: What must you do instead of squeezing inside the same lane alongside a pedestrian or cyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-F47.expected_back: Wait until an adjoining lane can be used safely rather than sharing a lane with a pedestrian or bicyclist.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: What should drivers on a multilane highway do when traffic is entering from an on-ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: On roads with multiple lanes, make room for another vehicle entering the roadway.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: Which unprotected road users need generous side clearance and alertness for sudden moves?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: Give pedestrians and bicyclists extra clearance and watch for children who can move suddenly.

sec12-card-sec12-F48.front: About how many seconds of open traffic gap does the guide recommend to merge, enter, or change lanes?
sec12-card-sec12-F48.expected_back: The guide recommends a gap of about four seconds for a lane change, roadway entry, or merge.

sec12-card-sec12-F49.front: How must you move across several highway lanes toward an exit or turn?
sec12-card-sec12-F49.expected_back: When moving across multiple lanes, complete one lane change at a time.

sec12-card-sec12-F50.front: Why must you reject squeezing into a tight traffic gap that barely fits your car?
sec12-card-sec12-F50.expected_back: Do not enter a gap so small that the available safety cushion can quickly disappear.

sec12-card-sec12-F51.front: When is it safe to treat a highway median crossover as a halfway waiting zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F51.expected_back: When crossing traffic, use a median as a waiting place only if it is large enough to contain your whole vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-F52.front: When must you hold back from starting a left turn even if oncoming lanes open up?
sec12-card-sec12-F52.expected_back: Do not begin a left turn while a vehicle or pedestrian blocks the path needed to complete it.

sec12-card-sec12-F53.front: What must you do at a green traffic light when backed-up cars block the far side of the intersection?
sec12-card-sec12-F53.expected_back: Even on green, wait outside an intersection until there is enough clear space to finish crossing.

sec12-card-sec12-F54.front: Why should you wait before pulling out in front of an oncoming car whose turn signal is blinking?
sec12-card-sec12-F54.expected_back: Do not rely only on an approaching vehicle's turn signal; wait for the vehicle to begin turning before starting your own safe turn.

sec12-card-sec12-F55.front: How many vehicles should you generally overtake per pass instead of stringing several together?
sec12-card-sec12-F55.expected_back: As a general practice, pass one vehicle at a time rather than assuming room exists to overtake several together.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: How much front and rear cushion do you create by centering your car inside a four-second gap?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Positioning your vehicle in the middle of a four-second traffic gap creates about two seconds of following space on each side according to the guide.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: Why is an oncoming motorcycle's flashing turn signal extra risky to trust?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: A motorcycle's turn signal may remain on because it does not cancel automatically.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: Which two everyday reasons explain why a blinking oncoming car still blasts straight past you?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: An approaching vehicle's signal may indicate a turn beyond your location or may have been left on after an earlier turn.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.front: Which two actions must your chosen cross-traffic gap cover when turning onto a fast road?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.expected_back: Entering traffic requires enough space both to make the turn and to reach traffic speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F56.front: What is the only right decision if you hesitate over whether time and space allow a pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F56.expected_back: If you are unsure there is enough space or time for a safe pass, wait for a larger gap.

sec12-card-sec12-F57.front: Within what distance of a hill or curve does the Arkansas guide forbid passing?
sec12-card-sec12-F57.expected_back: Do not pass within a third of a mile of a hill or curve according to the guide's stated restriction.

sec12-card-sec12-F58.front: Which three junction types must you avoid passing near because cross-traffic can enter?
sec12-card-sec12-F58.expected_back: Avoid passing where vehicles may cross or enter, including intersections, railroad crossings, and shopping-center entrances.

sec12-card-sec12-F59.front: What roadside or lane conditions ahead should you scan for before starting a pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F59.expected_back: Before passing, look for road obstructions or conditions that could push another vehicle into your intended lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F60.front: What must be waiting ahead of the vehicle you plan to pass before you ever pull out?
sec12-card-sec12-F60.expected_back: Do not begin a pass unless enough space remains to return safely to the normal driving lane.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.front: Roughly how many seconds and what opposing gap does a pass at fifty-five miles per hour require?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.expected_back: At fifty-five miles per hour, the guide describes needing roughly ten seconds of passing time and an equivalent gap in opposing traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.front: Why is it so hard to judge the closing speed of a distant oncoming vehicle on a straight road?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.expected_back: An oncoming vehicle far away can appear motionless, making its speed difficult to judge.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.front: What deadly hazards can the vehicle you are overtaking hide from view near a crossing?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.expected_back: A vehicle being overtaken can block your view of people, trains, or other road users near an intersection.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.front: What mirror cue confirms you have enough clearance to pull back right after a nighttime pass?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.expected_back: At night, the guide uses seeing both headlights of the overtaken vehicle in the rearview mirror as a return-to-lane spacing cue.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.front: What is the primary reserved purpose of the left lane on a multilane Arkansas highway?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.expected_back: Arkansas reserves the left lane of a multilane highway for passing, except for the specific other uses described in the guide.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.front: When does road construction legally allow continuous travel in the left highway lane?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.expected_back: Left-lane use is also allowed when every other same-direction lane is closed for construction or repair.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.front: What pavement or surface condition lets you legally stay in the left highway lane?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.expected_back: A driver may use the left lane when the other same-direction lanes are unsafe or undrivable.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.front: Which upcoming ramp maneuver permits moving into and holding the left highway lane?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.expected_back: Preparing for an exit on the left is another listed exception permitting left-lane use.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.front: Which roadside users or surface obstacles can suddenly wipe out the lane space you planned to pass in?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.expected_back: Pedestrians, bicyclists, narrow bridges, ice, potholes, or objects can eliminate the space a driver expected to use for passing.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: How does a tractor-trailer stopping distance compare with a passenger car traveling at the exact same speed?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: A tractor-trailer needs more stopping distance than a passenger car traveling at the same speed.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: Roughly what total stopping distance does the Arkansas guide give for an average passenger car moving at fifty-five miles per hour?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: At fifty-five miles per hour, the guide gives roughly two hundred twenty-five feet as the average passenger car's stopping distance.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.front: How much stopping distance can a fully loaded tractor-trailer need when traveling at fifty-five miles per hour?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.expected_back: A fully loaded tractor-trailer moving at fifty-five miles per hour can require over three hundred thirty-five feet to stop, according to the guide.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: When any vehicle turns a corner, how does the path of its rear wheels compare with its front wheels?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: A turning vehicle's rear wheels trace a tighter path than its front wheels, with a larger difference on longer vehicles.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: Why might a tractor-trailer swing toward the left before making a turn at an intersection?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: A tractor-trailer may first move left to create enough room for a right turn.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: What should you verify before trying to pass a large truck that begins shifting to the left?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: Before trying to pass a truck that appears to be moving left, check its turn signal and determine the intended turn.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: Why is it unsafe to expect a tractor-trailer to handle and maneuver like an oversized passenger car?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: A tractor-trailer is not simply a larger passenger car; its capabilities and normal maneuvers require different expectations from nearby drivers.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: Do a commercial driver's elevated seat and oversized mirrors get rid of serious blind spots around the rig?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: A truck driver's high seat and large mirrors do not eliminate the vehicle's serious blind spots.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: Within how much space directly ahead of a tractor-trailer cab can a passenger car disappear from the driver's view?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: A passenger car may be hidden from a tractor-trailer's driver within twenty feet ahead of the cab.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: Where do side blind spots stretch along a tractor-trailer, and where are they especially severe?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: Tractor-trailer blind spots extend along both sides, especially near the cab.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: How far behind a tractor-trailer can the rear blind area extend according to the Arkansas guide?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: The guide describes the blind area behind a tractor-trailer as extending as far as two hundred feet.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: How does hanging out beside or right behind a truck in its blind area affect the truck driver?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: Remaining beside or behind a truck in its blind area limits the truck driver's ability to avoid a hazard.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: What should you assume whenever you cannot see a truck driver's reflection in the rig's side mirror?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Use the truck's side mirror as a visibility cue: if you cannot see its driver in that mirror, assume the driver cannot see your vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: What visibility advantage and disadvantage come together from sitting up inside a tall truck cab?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: The truck cab offers a better forward view while leaving substantial blind areas immediately around the vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: Which three basic vehicle maneuvers require more space for a large truck than for a passenger car?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: Trucks need more room to stop, accelerate, and turn than passenger cars.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: What must you avoid doing with a truck's open front cushion when approaching an exit, turn, or lane closure?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Do not cut into the truck driver's safety space to reach an exit, turn, or lane closure ahead of the truck.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: How should you handle a highway exit when a large truck is already traveling right ahead in that lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Slow and take an exit behind a truck rather than racing to cut in front of it.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: Which side should you use to overtake a tractor-trailer, and how should you complete the pass?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: Pass a tractor-trailer on its left and complete the pass without lingering alongside.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: Why must you never follow closely behind a large truck in traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: Do not tailgate a truck, because close following removes your space to react to a sudden stop.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: Beyond sudden braking, what roadway hazard makes extra following clearance behind a high-clearance truck essential?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Give a truck enough following clearance to react if it strikes an object that could then hit your vehicle.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: Why do drivers need extra caution when judging an approaching tractor-trailer's speed from down the road?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: Judge the approach of a tractor-trailer carefully; its size can make it appear to move more slowly than it actually does.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: What does the open gap a truck driver leaves in front of the cab actually represent?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: A truck's open space ahead is a safety cushion, not an invitation for another driver to cut in.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: What specific problem do you create if you linger right alongside a truck during a pass?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: Lingering beside a passing truck can prevent its driver from maneuvering around an obstacle ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: Which two critical factors can a motorist easily misjudge when watching a large truck approach an intersection?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: At an intersection, a driver can misjudge both how close an approaching truck is and how rapidly it is arriving.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: How do a commercial truck's weight and handling responsiveness compare with a standard passenger car?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: A truck weighs much more than a car and cannot maneuver as readily.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: In the national comparison cited by the Arkansas guide, what share of fatal multivehicle tractor-trailer crashes is attributed to the passenger-car side?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: The guide attributes seventy-two percent of fatal multivehicle crashes involving a tractor-trailer to the passenger-car side in its cited national comparison.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: Which three personal conditions form the foundation for safe driving in the Arkansas guide?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Safe driving depends on clear vision, adequate rest, and avoiding alcohol or illegal drugs before driving.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: What three critical driving tasks depend directly on having clear sight?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: Clear sight is needed to identify traffic and road conditions, detect hazards, and react in time.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: What is peripheral vision, and how does it help while you are driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: Peripheral vision is the view from the corner of the eye that helps reveal vehicles or hazards beside you.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: Because peripheral vision lacks sharp focus, what two habits should supplement it?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: Because side vision does not provide sharp focus, supplement it with side-mirror checks and sideward glances.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: During which two high-stakes maneuvers is judging vehicle distance and speed especially crucial?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: Judging vehicle distances and speeds is important when choosing a merging gap or passing on a two-lane road.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: How should you adjust your driving habits if you struggle to see well after dark?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: If nighttime vision is poor, avoid unnecessary night driving and use extra care when it is necessary.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: How often does the Arkansas guide recommend having an eye specialist test your vision, and why?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: The guide recommends an eye-specialist examination each year because poor vision may go unnoticed without testing.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: What does Restriction B on an Arkansas driver license require whenever you are behind the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: Wear prescribed corrective lenses when driving; a license bearing restriction B requires the driver's eyewear.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: What practical eyewear precaution does the guide recommend keeping inside your vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: Keep a spare pair of glasses in the vehicle in case the usual pair is lost or forgotten.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: Why must you never wear sunglasses or tinted contact lenses while driving at night?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: Avoid dark or tinted glasses or contact lenses at night because they reduce the light available for seeing the road.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: Which three specific traffic sounds can warn an alert driver of nearby danger?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: Horns, sirens, and tire sounds can provide warnings about road danger.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: How can a deaf or hard-of-hearing motorist safely make up for missed sound cues?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: A deaf or hearing-impaired driver can compensate by relying on visual awareness.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: What enforcement consequence can follow if you drive without corrective lenses required on your license?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: Failing to wear corrective lenses required by the license can result in a traffic ticket.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: In what physical state should you start a long highway drive rather than leaving tired?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: Begin a long trip rested rather than departing while already tired.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: What two scheduling habits help you complete a long road trip safely?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: Plan breaks and allow enough time to finish a trip safely.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: Which time window should you avoid when scheduling a long drive?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: Avoid scheduling long drives during the hours when your body normally sleeps.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: What is the right move when drowsiness hits behind the wheel instead of gambling on staying awake?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: If sleepy, stop and sleep instead of gambling on remaining awake behind the wheel.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: How can minor ailments like a stiff neck, cough, or sore leg affect driving, and what should you do?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: Illness or even a stiff neck, cough, or sore leg can interfere with driving; have another person drive when you are unwell.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: Who should a motorist under treatment for a heart condition consult before getting behind the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: A driver being treated for a heart condition should ask the treating doctor before driving.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: How can intense feelings like worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness affect you on the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: Strong worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness can impair the ability to drive.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: What should you do before driving if you are heated with anger or overly worked up?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: If angry or excited, stay off the road until you have had time to calm down.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: How should a driver prone to impatience plan trips to avoid risky choices in traffic?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: An impatient driver should allow extra travel time rather than rushing and taking unsafe actions.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: Why does the Arkansas guide suggest eating lighter meals before setting out on a drive?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: The guide recommends lighter meals before a drive because a large meal can increase drowsiness.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: What three restorative things do scheduled highway breaks let a driver do?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: Breaks on a long trip provide an opportunity to leave the vehicle, walk, and rest.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: What precaution does the guide give a person whose body is still adjusting to an insulin dose?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: The guide advises someone adjusting to an insulin dose to have another person drive.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: Which specific insulin-related medical danger does the Arkansas guide warn must keep a driver off the road?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: The guide warns an insulin-using driver not to drive when there is a risk of the condition it calls diabetic shock.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: According to the Arkansas guide, how much alcohol concentration in the body is considered safe for driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: Do not drink alcohol and drive; the guide states that no alcohol concentration is safe for vehicle operation.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.front: Does years of driving experience protect a motorist from alcohol impairment compared with newer drivers?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.expected_back: Alcohol affects experienced drivers as well as new drivers, who are still developing their skills.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.front: Which essential driving ability is the very first one harmed after consuming alcohol?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.expected_back: Judgment is the first driving ability affected by alcohol.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.front: How does alcohol change your reaction speed, eyesight, and overall alertness?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.expected_back: Alcohol slows reactions, makes vision less clear, and reduces alertness.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.front: What happens to your decision-making and car-handling abilities as more alcohol builds up in your system?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.expected_back: Increasing alcohol in the body worsens judgment and vehicle-control skills.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.front: Which three attributes of other vehicles become harder to judge accurately under alcohol impairment?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.expected_back: Alcohol impairment can make it harder to judge another vehicle's distance, speed, and movement.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.front: What transportation plan should you set up before social drinking, and what if none is arranged?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.expected_back: Arrange a designated driver before drinking socially; without one, use a cab or public transportation.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.front: Should you drive after drinking if you still feel steady and confident in your control?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.expected_back: Do not drive after consuming alcohol, even if you believe you can still control the vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.front: Do coffee, cold showers, brisk air, or exercise sober an impaired person up faster?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.expected_back: Coffee, fresh air, exercise, and a cold shower do not provide a quick way to sober up.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.front: What does food in the stomach actually do to alcohol absorption, and does it stop intoxication?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.expected_back: Food can slow alcohol's entry into the bloodstream but does not prevent intoxication.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.front: What is the single thing that clears alcohol out of the human body?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.expected_back: Time is required for the body to eliminate alcohol; a quick sobering-up method is not available.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.front: What can happen to your driving privilege if you refuse a lawful alcohol test?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.expected_back: Refusing an alcohol test requested under the guide's described law can result in loss of the driver license.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: Beyond crash danger, what legal and financial penalties can follow a drinking-and-driving violation?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: Drinking-and-driving consequences can include fines, higher insurance costs, license loss, an ignition interlock requirement, or imprisonment.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: How does consumed alcohol travel through the body to disrupt safe driving?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: The guide describes alcohol traveling through the bloodstream to the brain and affecting areas responsible for judgment and skill.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: By the moment a drinker consciously feels buzzed, what has already happened to their driving judgment?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: By the time a person notices alcohol's effects, judgment can already be substantially impaired.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: What is the difference between blood alcohol concentration and breath alcohol concentration?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: Blood alcohol concentration describes alcohol in blood, while breath alcohol concentration describes alcohol measured in breath.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.front: Under what age is buying or consuming alcohol illegal in Arkansas?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.expected_back: Arkansas prohibits buying or consuming alcohol before age twenty-one.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.front: What fine range, maximum jail exposure, and license suspension apply to a first alcohol-violation conviction in the Arkansas guide?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.expected_back: The first alcohol-violation conviction described in the guide carries a fine from one hundred fifty to one thousand dollars plus court costs, with possible jail time of one year and suspension of the license for one hundred twenty days.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.front: How do penalties change for drivers convicted of subsequent alcohol violations?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.expected_back: The guide warns that later alcohol-violation convictions carry more severe consequences, potentially including prison.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.front: What fine and driver-license penalty can strike an underage driver convicted of an alcohol violation in the guide?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.expected_back: An underage alcohol conviction described in the guide can lead to a fine of two thousand dollars and loss of the license until age twenty-one.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.front: How can an alcohol purchase or possession conviction affect driving privileges for someone under twenty-one?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.expected_back: An alcohol-purchase or possession conviction for a person younger than twenty-one can result in suspension, revocation, or disqualification of driving privileges.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.front: Can legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines make you unsafe to drive?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.expected_back: Prescription and nonprescription medicines can impair driving, including by causing drowsiness.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.front: What two steps should you take before driving after starting any medication?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.expected_back: Before driving after medication use, read its warning label and ask a doctor or pharmacist about possible effects.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.front: Why must you never mix alcohol with prescription medicines or other drugs?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.expected_back: Do not combine alcohol with medicines or other drugs, because the effects may increase impairment and create serious health risks.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.front: After a brief burst of wakefulness, what dangerous side effects can stimulant or diet pills trigger?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.expected_back: Stimulant or diet pills can briefly make a driver feel alert and later cause nervousness, dizziness, poor concentration, or vision problems.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.front: Which four core driving abilities can other drugs impair in ways similar to alcohol?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.expected_back: Other drugs can impair reaction, judgment, sight, and alertness in ways resembling alcohol.

sec15-card-sec15-F40.front: What two major harms does the Arkansas guide link directly to illegal drug use?
sec15-card-sec15-F40.expected_back: Illegal drug use can impair safe driving as well as harm health.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: What routine habit best lowers your odds of facing a sudden mechanical breakdown on the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: Follow the maintenance schedule recommended in your vehicle's owner manual to reduce the chance of a mechanical emergency.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: In the brake-failure response described by the Arkansas guide, what should you try first with the brake pedal?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: For the brake failure described in the guide, first pump the pedal several times to try to restore enough pressure to stop.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: If pumping the foot pedal fails to restore braking, how should you use the parking brake?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: If pedal pumping does not restore failed brakes, the guide calls for gradual use of the parking brake to avoid locking the rear wheels.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: What must you stay ready to do while applying the parking brake during an emergency stop?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: Be ready to release the parking brake if its emergency use causes the vehicle to skid.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: If both pedal pumping and gradual parking-brake pressure fail to stop you, what should you do next?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: If the prior brake-failure measures do not work, shift progressively lower and seek a safe place off the roadway to stop.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: Once you bring a vehicle with failed brakes to a halt, may you keep driving it carefully?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: Do not continue driving a vehicle whose brakes have failed.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: What is your immediate steering priority the instant a tire blows out at speed?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: After a tire blowout, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle moving straight.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: How does the Arkansas guide instruct you to shed speed after a tire blowout?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.expected_back: For a blowout, reduce speed gradually by easing off the accelerator and using only light brake pressure as described by the guide.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: Where should you bring your vehicle to a complete stop after handling a blowout?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: After a blowout, leave the roadway for a safe stopping place instead of stopping in the travel lane if possible.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: How does steering feel if your engine stalls while moving, and how should you hold the wheel?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: If the engine fails, retain a firm steering grip because steering may become difficult even though the wheel can still turn.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: When an engine dies in traffic, where should you steer and what change should you expect at the brake pedal?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: With an engine failure, move off the road and expect the working brakes to need much more pedal force.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: What quick check should you try first if your headlights abruptly go dark at night?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: If headlights suddenly fail, try operating the light switch several times.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: If working the switch fails to bring dead headlights back, what lights should you use and where should you go?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: If switching does not restore failed headlights, activate available hazard flashers, turn signals, or fog lamps and pull off the road promptly.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: If your accelerator sticks and engine speed keeps climbing, what should you do first while watching the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: For an accelerator that keeps increasing engine speed, watch the road and quickly shift the transmission to neutral.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: After shifting to neutral for a runaway accelerator, in what exact order do you leave the road and cut the ignition?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: After shifting to neutral for a runaway accelerator, move off the road safely and then shut the engine off.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: Why must emergency parking-brake pressure be applied slowly rather than yanked all at once?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: The emergency parking-brake application should be slow so the rear wheels do not lock and start a skid.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: Which three emergency maneuvers does the Arkansas guide list as options to avoid an imminent crash?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: In a threatened collision, the guide identifies stopping, steering away, and accelerating as possible avoidance choices.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.front: Where should you check to learn how your specific vehicle's antilock braking system operates?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.expected_back: Read the owner manual to understand how the vehicle's antilock braking system should be used.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.front: How should you use the brake pedal during an urgent stop in an ABS-equipped vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.expected_back: For an urgent stop with ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and maintain pressure.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.front: What must you avoid doing when an active ABS brake pedal vibrates or pushes back against your foot?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.expected_back: Do not release ABS brake pressure just because the pedal pushes back while the system operates.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.front: How should you brake urgently in a vehicle that does not have antilock brakes?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.expected_back: Without ABS, brake as strongly as possible without locking the wheels.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.front: In a non-ABS car, what should you do if hard braking locks the wheels and starts a skid?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.expected_back: If a non-ABS vehicle starts skidding because its wheels locked, promptly ease brake pressure, then reapply it after the skid ends.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.front: How should your hands hold the steering wheel when swerving away from a sudden collision threat?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.expected_back: Keep both hands on the steering wheel while steering away from a collision threat.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.front: After swerving past an initial hazard, what immediate control task remains?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.expected_back: After avoiding one hazard by steering away, be prepared to control the vehicle so it does not enter another collision.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.front: What three-part sequence does the guide describe for making an emergency quick turn without ABS?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.expected_back: For a quick turn without ABS, the guide describes braking first, releasing brake pressure, and then steering without locking the front wheels.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.front: Under what exact traffic conditions can accelerating help you avoid a crash?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.memory_hook: Side or rear threat, clear ahead
sec16-card-sec16-F25.expected_back: Acceleration can be an avoidance option when a side or rear collision threatens and clear space exists ahead.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.front: What should you do right after accelerating clear of an immediate collision threat?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.expected_back: After accelerating out of an immediate collision threat, reduce speed once the danger has passed.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.front: Which surface conditions and driver inputs raise the risk of throwing a vehicle into a skid?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.expected_back: Water, snow, ice, excessive speed, and sudden turns or stops can increase the risk of skidding.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.front: Where should you aim and steer your front wheels if your vehicle starts skidding?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.expected_back: If the vehicle skids, steer toward the path you want the vehicle to follow.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.front: What steering adjustment must you make right as a skidding car starts straightening back out?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.expected_back: As a skidding vehicle begins to straighten, correct the steering back so it does not swing into a new skid in the opposite direction.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.front: How long must you keep making smooth steering adjustments during a skid?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.expected_back: Continue controlled steering corrections until the vehicle's grip and control return.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: What crucial control capability does ABS preserve while you brake hard in an emergency?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: ABS permits steering during a braking maneuver according to the guide's emergency-avoidance instructions.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: What physical event between your vehicle and the pavement defines a skid?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: A skid occurs when tires lose their grip on the roadway.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: What does the Arkansas guide's skid-recovery section warn against doing with the brake pedal?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: The guide's skid-recovery instructions warn that applying brakes can make a skid worse.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.front: When is an uninvolved passing motorist allowed to stop at a roadside crash scene?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.expected_back: Do not stop to look at a crash unless you are involved or emergency assistance has not yet arrived.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.front: Why must drivers stay away from crash, fire, or disaster scenes they are not part of?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.expected_back: Do not drive toward an accident, fire, or disaster scene where your vehicle could obstruct responders.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.front: What two immediate positioning steps must you take if you are involved in a traffic crash?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.expected_back: If you are involved in a crash, stop at or near the scene and move the vehicle out of traffic if possible.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.front: Where should people stand or wait after a collision instead of lingering on the roadway?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.expected_back: After a crash, stay out of travel lanes rather than standing or walking where another vehicle could strike you.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.front: What two fire precautions must be taken around wrecked vehicles right after a crash?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.expected_back: Switch off the ignition of wrecked vehicles and avoid smoking near them because fuel may have spilled.

sec16-card-sec16-F36.front: How should everyone at a crash scene treat electrical wires knocked down onto the ground?
sec16-card-sec16-F36.expected_back: Keep away from electrical wires brought down at a crash scene.

sec16-card-sec16-F37.front: What hazard must you keep in mind when placing warning devices to alert approaching traffic at a wreck?
sec16-card-sec16-F37.expected_back: Warn approaching traffic using suitable warning devices while taking spilled fuel and fire risk into account.

sec16-card-sec16-F38.front: What crucial details should you give emergency responders when reporting a crash?
sec16-card-sec16-F38.expected_back: Notify emergency responders of the crash's precise location and hazards such as fire, fuel spills, or fallen electrical wires.

sec16-card-sec16-F39.front: Under what sole circumstance should you move an injured crash victim before paramedics arrive?
sec16-card-sec16-F39.expected_back: Do not move an injured person unless a burning vehicle or another immediate danger makes remaining in place unsafe.

sec16-card-sec16-F40.front: What basic first-aid step does the Arkansas guide recommend to slow or stop wound bleeding?
sec16-card-sec16-F40.expected_back: The guide recommends direct pressure on a bleeding wound to slow or stop the bleeding.

sec16-card-sec16-F41.front: Should you offer water or anything else to drink to an injured person waiting for paramedics?
sec16-card-sec16-F41.expected_back: Do not give an injured person anything to drink, including water, before medical personnel arrive.

sec16-card-sec16-F42.front: How does the guide advise helping protect an injured crash victim against medical shock?
sec16-card-sec16-F42.expected_back: The guide recommends covering an injured person with a blanket or warm clothing to help protect against shock.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: What should you attempt to do right away if your vehicle strikes a parked car?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: If you collide with a parked vehicle, try to find its owner.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.front: Which crashes require immediate police notification under the Arkansas guide?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.expected_back: The guide requires immediate police notification for a crash involving injury, death, or property damage exceeding one thousand dollars.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.front: After a crash involving injury or death, how long must involved drivers stay at the scene?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.expected_back: After a crash causing injury or death, remain until police have spoken with the drivers and obtained the information they need.

sec16-card-sec16-R16.front: When helping a crash victim who is unconscious or unable to move, what two checks should you perform in order?
sec16-card-sec16-R16.expected_back: When assisting someone unconscious or unable to move, the guide directs a check for breathing followed by a check for bleeding.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.front: For which three categories of people at a crash scene should you write down names and addresses?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.expected_back: Record names and addresses for people involved in the crash, injured people, and witnesses.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.front: What four personal and coverage items should involved drivers exchange with one another?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.expected_back: Exchange driver names, addresses, license numbers, and available insurance policy details with the other involved drivers.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.front: Which five specific details about the involved vehicles should you record after a collision?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.expected_back: Record involved vehicles' plate numbers, make, model, year, and visible damage.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.front: How must you respond when police or emergency officials ask for crash information?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.expected_back: Provide requested crash information to police or other emergency officials.

sec16-card-sec16-R12.front: When must a collision be reported to the Arkansas Office of Driver Services?
sec16-card-sec16-R12.expected_back: A crash involving injury, death, or more than three thousand dollars of damage to one person's property must be reported to the Office of Driver Services under the guide's reporting rule.

sec16-card-sec16-R13.front: Within what deadline after a qualifying crash must the report to the Office of Driver Services be filed?
sec16-card-sec16-R13.expected_back: The report to the Office of Driver Services must be filed within thirty days after the crash.

sec16-card-sec16-R14.front: Who may file the required crash report if injuries keep the driver from completing it personally?
sec16-card-sec16-R14.expected_back: If injury prevents a driver from completing the required crash report, another person may submit it on that driver's behalf.

sec16-card-sec16-R15.front: Where can Arkansas motorists pick up official crash-report forms?
sec16-card-sec16-R15.expected_back: Crash-report forms are available through Driver Services offices and most insurance agents.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: When a police officer signals you to pull over, how should you signal and where should you move?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: When a police officer signals you to stop, use your turn signal and move toward a safe stopping place on the right.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What three actions should you take if you are unsure whether the person signaling you to stop is a real police officer?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: If you doubt that the person stopping you is a police officer, signal, stop at the nearest well-lit location, and call nine one one to confirm the officer's identity.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: When choosing where to pull over for a traffic stop, what roadway structures should you avoid?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: For a traffic stop, leave the traffic lane at the nearest safe place and avoid stopping on a bridge or overpass.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: During a traffic stop, when should you step out of your vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: During a traffic stop, stay inside your vehicle until the officer directs you to get out.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Where should your hands be as an officer walks up to your window during a traffic stop?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Keep both hands where an approaching officer can see them, such as at the top of the steering wheel.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: What kind of body movement must you avoid when getting your paperwork during a traffic stop?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: Avoid abrupt movements when searching for documents during a traffic stop.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: Which vehicle light should you turn on right away when pulled over after dark?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: At a nighttime traffic stop, switch on the vehicle's interior lights to help the officer see inside.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: What should you do with your car stereo and phone as soon as you pull over for an officer?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: Give the officer your attention by silencing the radio and putting mobile devices down.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: What three pieces of information should the officer share with you during a traffic stop?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: The stopping officer should identify their name and agency and explain the reason for the stop.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Which three documents must you hand over when an officer asks for them during a stop?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: At an officer's request, provide your driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: What two steps should you take before reaching into a pocket, bag, or glovebox for requested documents?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: Before reaching for documents, tell the officer where they are and ask permission to retrieve them.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: If there is a weapon inside your vehicle during a traffic stop, how must you handle telling the officer and your hands?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: If your vehicle contains a weapon, tell the officer its type and location, do not reach for it, and obey the officer's instructions.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: What extra card should a concealed-carry permit holder hand over alongside their driver license at a traffic stop?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: A person holding a concealed-carry permit should show that permit with their driver license during a traffic stop.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: Which side of your car might an officer walk up to during a roadside traffic stop?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: An officer may approach either side of your vehicle, choosing the side that is safest.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: How should you act during a traffic stop even if you think the officer is wrong?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: Remain courteous during a traffic stop even when you disagree with the officer's actions.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: Where is the proper place to contest a traffic citation if you believe it was unfair?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.memory_hook: Contest tickets in court, never roadside
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: Challenge a citation through the court named on it rather than arguing beside the roadway.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: What does signing a traffic citation legally mean, and does it admit guilt?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: Signing a required citation promises a court appearance or payment before the court date; it does not admit guilt.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: What three serious consequences can follow if you refuse to sign a required traffic citation?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: Refusing a required citation signature can lead to arrest, a bond requirement, and possible impoundment of the vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: Should a passing motorist or pedestrian walk up to an officer who is conducting someone else's traffic stop?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: Do not approach an officer conducting a traffic stop that does not involve you.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: How must you drive past a stopped police car or authorized roadside vehicle, and what is your backup move if lanes are blocked?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: When passing a stopped officer or another authorized roadside vehicle, move as far away as possible; if changing lanes is unsafe or impossible, slow down and pass cautiously.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: Which age and body-weight combination requires a child passenger to ride in a properly attached child safety seat?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.memory_hook: Under six and under sixty pounds
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: A child younger than six who weighs less than sixty pounds must ride in a child safety seat that is properly attached to the vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Up to what age must children use appropriate safety restraints whenever a vehicle is in motion?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: Children younger than fifteen must use suitable safety restraints whenever their vehicle is moving.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: At what passenger age is knowingly smoking tobacco inside a motor vehicle prohibited in Arkansas?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: Knowingly smoking tobacco in a motor vehicle is prohibited whenever a child younger than fourteen is riding as a passenger.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: Which adult occupants must wear a seat belt under Arkansas's standard passenger-car rule?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: Arkansas requires a seat belt for the driver and the passenger in the front seat.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: When is it acceptable to leave a child or pet unattended inside a parked vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: Never leave a child or pet alone inside a vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: Does blasting the air conditioning before parking keep an empty car cool after you shut it off and walk away?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: Air conditioning used before parking does not keep the vehicle cool after you leave it.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: On a ninety-degree Fahrenheit day, how fast does a parked car's cabin climb back up to that outdoor temperature?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.memory_hook: Matches ninety degrees in five minutes
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: On a day with an outside temperature of ninety degrees Fahrenheit, the guide says the vehicle interior reaches the outdoor temperature within five minutes.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: By how many degrees Fahrenheit does the guide say a parked vehicle's interior keeps rising every nine minutes?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.memory_hook: Plus fifteen degrees every nine minutes
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: The guide describes the temperature inside a parked vehicle rising another fifteen degrees Fahrenheit for each nine-minute interval.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.front: What maximum fine does the Arkansas guide state for a seat-belt violation, before possible court costs or fees?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.expected_back: The seat-belt penalty described in the guide is a fine of no more than twenty-five dollars, with court costs or fees also possible.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.front: What option does the guide mention for families who cannot afford to buy a child safety seat?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.expected_back: Some organizations lend child safety seats to people who cannot afford to buy them.

sec02-card-sec02-R17.front: When it is seventy degrees Fahrenheit outside, what temperatures does a parked car hit after ten minutes and thirty minutes?
sec02-card-sec02-R17.expected_back: With an outside temperature of seventy degrees Fahrenheit, the guide's parked-vehicle example reaches eighty-nine degrees after ten minutes and one hundred four degrees after thirty minutes.

sec02-card-sec02-R18.front: At seventy-five degrees Fahrenheit outdoors, what cabin temperatures does the parked-car example reach at ten and thirty minutes?
sec02-card-sec02-R18.expected_back: At seventy-five degrees Fahrenheit outdoors, the guide's parked-vehicle example reaches ninety-four degrees after ten minutes and one hundred nine degrees after thirty minutes.

sec02-card-sec02-R19.front: When outdoor air is eighty degrees Fahrenheit, what interior temperatures develop inside a parked vehicle at ten and thirty minutes?
sec02-card-sec02-R19.expected_back: At an outdoor temperature of eighty degrees Fahrenheit, the parked-vehicle example reaches ninety-nine degrees after ten minutes and one hundred fourteen degrees after thirty minutes.

sec02-card-sec02-R20.front: With eighty-five-degree Fahrenheit outdoor air, how hot does a parked vehicle get after ten minutes and after thirty minutes?
sec02-card-sec02-R20.memory_hook: Eighty-five hits hundred four, hundred nineteen
sec02-card-sec02-R20.expected_back: With eighty-five-degree-Fahrenheit outdoor air, the guide's example reaches one hundred four degrees inside the parked vehicle after ten minutes and one hundred nineteen degrees after thirty minutes.

sec02-card-sec02-R21.front: At ninety degrees Fahrenheit outside, what cabin temperatures does a parked car reach at ten minutes and thirty minutes?
sec02-card-sec02-R21.memory_hook: Ninety hits hundred nine, hundred twenty-four
sec02-card-sec02-R21.expected_back: At ninety degrees Fahrenheit outside, the example shows a parked vehicle reaching one hundred nine degrees after ten minutes and one hundred twenty-four degrees after thirty minutes.

sec02-card-sec02-R22.front: When outdoor air reaches ninety-five degrees Fahrenheit, what temperatures build inside a parked car at ten and thirty minutes?
sec02-card-sec02-R22.memory_hook: Ninety-five hits hundred fourteen, hundred twenty-nine
sec02-card-sec02-R22.expected_back: When outdoor air is ninety-five degrees Fahrenheit, the example reaches one hundred fourteen degrees inside after ten minutes and one hundred twenty-nine degrees after thirty minutes.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: Where must you steer when an emergency vehicle approaches with sirens or air horns and flashing red or blue lights?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: For an approaching emergency vehicle using its siren or air horn and red or blue flashing lights, pull toward the roadway's right edge.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: What should you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are already inside an intersection?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.memory_hook: Clear the intersection, then pull right
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in an intersection, finish crossing the intersection before pulling aside.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: On a multilane highway, which lane should you take when passing a stopped police vehicle flashing emergency lights?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: On a multilane highway, change to the lane farthest from a stopped police vehicle displaying emergency lights whenever that lane change is possible.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Which directions of traffic must make a full stop for a stopped school bus flashing red lights, absent a wide median?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: Stop completely for a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights, whether you approach from behind, the opposite direction, or an intersection, unless the stated median exception applies.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: After stopping for a school bus loading or unloading students, when are you allowed to drive past?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: Do not pass a school bus loading or unloading passengers until it moves again with its flashing red lights off.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: How wide must a dividing median be before oncoming traffic does not have to stop for a school bus's flashing red lights?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: Traffic approaching a school bus from the opposite direction need not stop when the opposing travel lanes are separated by a median at least twenty feet wide.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: What are school buses required to do at every railroad grade crossing?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: School buses must stop for every railroad crossing.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: Who must stop for a school bus flashing red lights when the median separating opposing lanes is narrower than twenty feet?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.memory_hook: Under twenty feet, all lanes stop
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: When the median separating opposing traffic is narrower than twenty feet, every traffic lane must stop for the school bus's flashing red lights.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: What criminal offense category can apply to illegally passing a stopped school bus displaying flashing red lights?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: Illegally passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights can be punished as a misdemeanor.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: What criminal charge category applies when someone ignores the school-bus stopping law and causes a fatal crash?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: A driver who disobeys the school-bus stopping law and causes someone's death faces a felony charge.

sec02-card-sec02-F46.front: Which four categories of stopped flashing-light vehicles trigger the multilane move-over rule on Arkansas highways?
sec02-card-sec02-F46.expected_back: On a multilane highway, move to the farthest available lane from a stopped enforcement, transportation-department, utility, or towing vehicle displaying its lights.

sec02-card-sec02-R23.front: What fine range and potential jail term apply to an illegal school-bus passing conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-R23.expected_back: The school-bus passing violation described in the guide carries a fine ranging from two hundred fifty to one thousand dollars, possible jail time of up to ninety days, or both.

sec02-card-sec02-R24.front: Under Isaac's Law, what specific felony charge applies to negligently causing someone's death by violating the school-bus stop law?
sec02-card-sec02-R24.expected_back: Isaac's Law is described as making a negligent death caused by the specified violation Class C felony negligent homicide.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.front: Who are designated accessible parking spaces legally reserved for?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.expected_back: An accessible parking space is reserved for a person whose disability qualifies under state law.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.front: Which two vehicle credentials authorize parking in an accessible space?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.expected_back: Using an accessible parking space requires the appropriate disability license plate or designated special-certificate hangtag.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.front: When can a disability parking special certificate legally move from one vehicle to another?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.expected_back: The disability parking special certificate can move between vehicles only when its disabled owner is present.

sec02-card-sec02-F42.front: Who must be inside the vehicle whenever a disability special certificate is used to park in an accessible stall?
sec02-card-sec02-F42.expected_back: When using an accessible parking space, the person to whom the special certificate belongs must be present in the vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-F43.front: Where inside your parked vehicle must you display a disability parking special certificate?
sec02-card-sec02-F43.expected_back: Display the disability parking certificate on the rearview mirror or dashboard.

sec02-card-sec02-F44.front: What must the certificate holder or disability-plated vehicle owner actually do when parking in an accessible stall?
sec02-card-sec02-F44.expected_back: The certificate holder or registered owner of the appropriately plated vehicle must leave the vehicle when the designated accessible space is used.

sec02-card-sec02-F45.front: What identification must you carry on you while using an accessible parking space?
sec02-card-sec02-F45.expected_back: Carry the issued or endorsed photo identification card on your person while using an accessible parking space.

sec02-card-sec02-R25.front: How does ownership of a disability license plate differ from ownership of a disability special certificate?
sec02-card-sec02-R25.expected_back: The guide distinguishes a disability license plate issued to a vehicle's registered owner from a special certificate issued to the individual with the disability.

sec02-card-sec02-R26.front: What criminal offense classification applies to fraudulently using someone else's disability parking certificate?
sec02-card-sec02-R26.memory_hook: Placard fraud is Class A misdemeanor
sec02-card-sec02-R26.expected_back: Fraudulent use of someone else's disability parking certificate can result in a Class A misdemeanor.

sec02-card-sec02-R27.front: What fine range applies to a first offense of misusing a disability parking certificate?
sec02-card-sec02-R27.memory_hook: First misuse costs hundred to five-hundred
sec02-card-sec02-R27.expected_back: The guide states a first-offense disability-certificate misuse fine ranging from one hundred to five hundred dollars.

sec02-card-sec02-R28.front: What fine range and driver-license penalty hit on a second offense of disability-certificate misuse?
sec02-card-sec02-R28.expected_back: For a second disability-certificate misuse offense, the guide gives a fine from two hundred fifty to one thousand dollars and suspension of the driver license for six months.

sec02-card-sec02-R29.front: Who has to pay the towing, impoundment, legal, and court costs tied to disability-certificate misuse?
sec02-card-sec02-R29.expected_back: The vehicle owner is responsible for the towing, impoundment, legal, court, and related costs described for disability-certificate misuse.

sec02-card-sec02-R30.front: Within how many days after moving away or a holder's death must a disability special certificate be returned, and to which office?
sec02-card-sec02-R30.expected_back: A disability parking special certificate must be returned to the Motor Vehicles Special Division within thirty days after moving or death.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: What must a commercial hauler do when transporting garbage, trash, or litter on Arkansas roads?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: A person hauling garbage, trash, or litter commercially must cover the load so material cannot escape from the vehicle.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: What duty applies when an everyday driver hauls their own household trash or litter?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: Someone carrying their own garbage, trash, or litter must take reasonable measures to keep the load from falling, blowing, or dropping out.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: When is a load made mostly of metal allowed to travel without a tarp or cover?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: A load consisting mainly of metal need not be covered if its loading method prevents the metal from dropping or falling off.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: Where is it illegal to abandon junk cars, old tires, discarded appliances, or their parts?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: Do not leave junk vehicles, used tires, abandoned appliances, or their parts on a highway right-of-way, other public property, or private land you do not control, except at the lawful facilities described in the guide.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: Which three types of lawful businesses or sites accept junk vehicles, used tires, and old appliances?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: The listed lawful facilities for discarded vehicles, tires, and appliances include a salvage yard, permitted disposal location, or a demolisher's business premises.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: When trash is tossed from any motor vehicle besides a motor bus, who does Arkansas law initially presume threw it?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: Litter deposited from a motor vehicle other than a motor bus is treated as initial evidence that the driver deposited it.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: What fine range and maximum community service apply to a first Arkansas littering conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: For a first littering conviction under the provisions described on this page, the guide gives a fine from one hundred to one thousand dollars and up to eight hours of community service.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: What fine range and community-service cap apply to a second littering conviction within three years?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: For another such littering conviction within three years of the first, the guide gives a fine from two hundred to two thousand dollars and possible community service of up to twenty-four hours.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Alongside fines and service hours, what hands-on task can a court order a littering offender to perform?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: A littering violator may also be directed to remove litter beside highways or from other designated places.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: How does Arkansas law name and classify littering done as part of running a business?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: Littering committed in furtherance of a commercial enterprise is described as commercial littering and a Class A misdemeanor.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: What exact fine and community-service penalty hit on a first offense of illegally dumping junk cars, tires, or appliances?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: For a first violation of the described rule against discarding certain large items, the guide states a one thousand-dollar fine and one hundred hours of community service.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.front: How is a repeat offense of illegally discarding junk vehicles, used tires, or abandoned appliances classified?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.memory_hook: Repeat large dumping, Class A misdemeanor
sec02-card-sec02-R12.expected_back: A repeat violation of the described rule against discarding certain large items is a Class A misdemeanor.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.front: Under what deal can a judge suspend part or all of a person's listed littering penalties?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.expected_back: A judge may suspend some or all listed littering penalties if the violator agrees to collect litter at designated places for a prescribed period.

sec02-card-sec02-R14.front: What happens to your driver license if you fail to pay court-assessed littering fines?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.expected_back: Failure to pay court-assessed littering fines under the cited provisions can produce a six-month license suspension after the court's order reaches the Department of Finance and Administration.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: What jobs do painted pavement lines and roadway symbols perform for drivers?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Pavement lines and symbols separate lanes and identify passing, turning, stopping, and pedestrian-crossing locations.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: What boundary does a solid white stripe painted along the side of the road mark?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: The solid white line at the roadside marks the roadway's outside edge.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: What traffic flow and lane-change rule does a broken white lane line indicate?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: A broken white lane line separates traffic moving in the same direction and may be crossed for a safe lane change.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: Under what condition are you allowed to cross a broken yellow center line to pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: A broken yellow center line permits passing across it when opposing traffic is absent and passing is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What passing rule applies when double solid yellow lines divide opposing lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Double solid yellow lines divide opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: When is crossing a solid yellow center line permitted for turning into a driveway?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: A solid yellow center line may be crossed for a driveway turn when no opposing vehicle is approaching the turn location.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: Which turning movement is a two-way shared center turn lane built to handle?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: A shared center turn lane serves left turns for traffic traveling in either direction.
