sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: How may a driver turning left out of a driveway or side street use a shared center turn lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: A driver turning left from a driveway or side street may use the shared center turn lane as part of entering or merging with traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Are you allowed to build up speed inside a shared center left-turn lane to merge into traffic?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: The shared center left-turn lane must not be used to accelerate into traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: What arrow pattern on the pavement marks a shared center turn lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: Shared center turn lanes have alternating left-turn arrows for vehicles arriving from opposite directions.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: What controls driving, passing, and turning when pavement markings and lane posts are missing?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: When lane-use signs and markings are absent, the general lane rules still govern driving, passing, and turning.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: What does Arkansas law say about backing your vehicle inside an active travel lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Backing a vehicle in a travel lane is both unsafe and illegal.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: What is the right move right after you accidentally pass your highway exit or street turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: After missing an exit or turn, keep going until a safe place to turn around is available rather than backing up.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: Where must you go if you need to check directions, handle car trouble, or drop off a passenger?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Do not stop in a travel lane to handle confusion, a breakdown, or a passenger drop-off; pull safely off the road.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Which lane should you normally use on a roadway with three or more lanes moving your direction?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: On a road with at least three same-direction lanes, use the right lane except when passing.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Which lane does the Arkansas guide recommend on a three-or-more-lane road when heavy traffic is merging?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: When substantial merging traffic is present on a road with at least three same-direction lanes, the guide recommends the center travel lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: Under what lone exception are you allowed to drive along a road shoulder?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: Driving on the shoulder is prohibited unless a police officer directs you to do so.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: May you ever use a paved or unpaved road shoulder to overtake another vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Never use the shoulder to pass another vehicle, whether the shoulder is paved or unpaved.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: What is the purpose of the far-left lane on a multilane roadway?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: On a multilane roadway, the far-left lane is intended for overtaking slower vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: Why does overtaking on the shoulder catch other drivers completely off guard?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Passing on the shoulder is dangerous because another driver may pull onto that shoulder without expecting a vehicle there.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: Which lane is designated for passing slower traffic when you are driving on a multi-lane road?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: When overtaking vehicles on a multi-lane road, the far-left lane is meant for passing slower vehicles.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: Which lane must you turn into when no turning signs or lane markings guide the intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Without turning-control signs or lane markings, turn into the lane nearest your direction of travel.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: What lane mistake must you avoid while making a right turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: Keep a right turn from swinging into the opposing traffic lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: Why must you avoid cutting the corner short during a left turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: Do not cut the corner during a left turn, because a sharply cut turn can strike a vehicle approaching from the left.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How should you position your car when an oncoming driver is also waiting to turn left?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Leave space for an oncoming vehicle to make its own left turn in front of you.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: What should you do instead of cruising right beside another vehicle on a multilane road?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: When another vehicle is traveling beside you on a multilane road, move ahead of it or fall behind it rather than remaining alongside.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: How should you handle a tailgater on a multilane road when the lane to your right is open?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: If a vehicle follows too closely on a multilane road, move into the lane to your right when that lane is clear.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: How can swinging wide to start a right turn confuse a driver following behind you?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: A wide right turn may mislead a following driver into thinking you are moving left, prompting that driver to try passing on your right.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: Where must your vehicle come to a full halt when a stop post has a painted stop line?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: When approaching a stop sign with a marked stop line, bring your vehicle to a complete stop before reaching the line.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: Which pedestrians at a crosswalk require you to yield?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Yield to a pedestrian who is already in a crosswalk or is about to enter it.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Why must you scan for people on foot even at intersections that lack painted crosswalk lines?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: Crosswalks are not always marked, so watch for pedestrians even at intersections without painted crosswalks.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What kind of priority belongs to a pedestrian walking with a guide dog or white cane?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: A pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane must receive absolute right of way.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: What should you turn on whenever spotting other road users starts getting tough?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Switch on headlights whenever seeing other road users becomes difficult so they can also see you.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: What lighting law kicks in whenever you need your windshield wipers in Arkansas?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Arkansas requires headlights whenever windshield-wiper use is necessary.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: Which sunset and sunrise time cutoffs mark required headlight hours in the guide?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: The guide identifies half an hour after sunset and half an hour before sunrise as headlight-use time points.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: At what unclear sight distance must you switch your headlights on regardless of time?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Use headlights whenever a person or object cannot be clearly seen within five hundred feet.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Is it legal to cruise down the road using only your parking lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Driving with only parking lights is illegal; parking lights are intended for a parked vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: When should you switch to high beams to stretch your forward view at night?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Use high beams when there are no approaching vehicles to improve the distance visible ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Within what distance of an oncoming vehicle must you drop from high beams to low?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Change from high to low beams when an approaching vehicle comes within five hundred feet.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: Within what following distance behind another vehicle must you use low beams?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: When following another vehicle at a distance under two hundred feet, use low beams.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Which headlight setting belongs in fog, snow, or heavy rain, and why?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Use low beams in fog, snowfall, or heavy rain, because high-beam reflection produces glare.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: What dual safety role do headlights perform during night driving?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Headlights help the driver see at night while also making the vehicle more visible to others.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Roughly how much farther ahead do high beams reach compared with low beams?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: The guide describes high beams as providing roughly twice the viewing distance of low beams.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: In which three night settings does the guide urge high beams when no traffic opposes you?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: The guide recommends high-beam use on unfamiliar roads, in construction areas, or where people may be near the roadside when opposing traffic is absent.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Which weather conditions are auxiliary fog lamps built to handle?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: Some vehicles have fog lamps designed for fog, rain, or snow.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: What is the proper reason to sound your horn rather than venting frustration?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: Use the horn to warn another road user about a dangerous situation rather than as an expression of annoyance.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: When is a horn tap appropriate around a pedestrian or bicyclist?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: A horn warning is appropriate when a pedestrian or cyclist appears about to enter your travel lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: What horn warning should you give if a car you are overtaking starts drifting into your lane?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: Warn with the horn when a driver you are passing begins moving into your lane.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: When should you sound a horn warning toward a distracted or inattentive driver?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: The guide recommends a horn warning when an inattentive driver has not seen your vehicle.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: Which urgent roadside or traffic threats call for a sharp blast of the horn?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Sound a sharp blast of the horn whenever a child or senior is poised to step, run, or ride onto the roadway, or whenever another vehicle risks colliding with yours.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: What horn action does the guide call for if your car slides out of control toward people or traffic?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: If you lose control toward pedestrians or opposing traffic, the guide calls for a sharp horn warning.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: Which three everyday social or impatient uses of the horn does the guide forbid?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Do not use the horn to urge a driver to go faster, criticize a mistake, or greet a friend.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Should you ever honk your horn at a blind pedestrian crossing or walking nearby?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Do not sound the horn at a blind pedestrian.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: What three situations do your hazard flashers warn approaching drivers about?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Hazard flashers warn other drivers of an emergency, a breakdown, or a vehicle stopped beside the roadway.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: How should you report a roadside breakdown when you have access to a phone?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: When a breakdown needs reporting, use an available phone and look for roadside signs identifying the emergency number to call.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: Why must you signal or tap brakes before turning, changing lanes, or slowing?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: Warn other drivers before changing direction or slowing so they have time to react.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: At least how far ahead must you signal before turning, merging, changing lanes, or parking?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: The guide calls for a turn signal at least one hundred feet before a lane change, turn, merge, or parking maneuver.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: When should you flick on your blinker if your driveway turn sits just past a cross street?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: If your planned turn is after an intersection, wait until you have crossed that intersection before signaling so another driver does not mistake your intended turn.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: When should you signal if a car waits to pull out between you and your upcoming turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: If another vehicle could enter the street between you and your intended turn, pass that vehicle's entry point before signaling the turn.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: What must you check on your dashboard right after finishing a lane change or gentle turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: Cancel a turn signal after completing the turn or lane change so it does not give others a false message.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: Which three blind terrain features does the guide name as smart places for a horn warning?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: The guide lists an obstructed view near a steep hill, sharp curve, or narrow-valley exit among situations for a horn warning.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: How do you switch on your vehicle's four-way emergency flashers?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Pressing the hazard-light control activates the emergency flashers.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: What happens to the pavement distance needed to slow or stop as speed climbs?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: Higher speed increases the distance needed to slow down or stop.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: Which three factors must govern your chosen driving speed at all times?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: Adjust speed to road and traffic conditions, remain aware of surrounding traffic, and obey posted limits.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: Where should you finish slowing down for an upcoming curve?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: Slow before a curve rather than relying on braking after entering it.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: What happens when you carry too much speed into a sharp curve?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: Taking a curve too fast can overcome tire grip and cause the vehicle to skid.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: How must shallow or worn tire tread change your speed on wet or icy pavement?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: Worn tire tread makes wet or icy driving more dangerous, requiring a speed below the posted maximum when conditions demand it.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: What should you do right away when rain, snow, or sleet starts falling?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: At the first rain, snow, or sleet, reduce speed because the road surface may become slippery.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: By how much does the Arkansas guide tell you to cut your speed on packed snow?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: On packed snow, the guide recommends reducing your speed by half.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: What is the guide's advice if roads ice over and you end up on ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: Avoid driving on icy roads if possible, and slow to a coast if driving on ice.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: What should you do when sheet glare ice turns the roadway dangerously slick?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: If glare ice makes the road extremely slippery, stop driving as soon as a safe opportunity is available.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: Why can tree-lined or shaded pavement still hide ice after sunlit lanes dry out?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: Ice may remain in shaded areas on cold, wet days because those spots freeze early and thaw late.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: Why must you watch bridges and overpasses closely during freezing weather?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: Bridges and overpasses may develop ice before adjoining pavement and can stay icy while the approaches appear clear.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: How does fresh ice right around freezing compare with deep-freeze ice?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: Fresh ice near the freezing point can be more slippery than ice at much lower temperatures.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: Why are the opening minutes of a summer rainstorm extra slick?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: On a hot day, the first minutes of rain can be particularly slick as oil reaches the surface before it washes away.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How many total feet does an average passenger car need to stop from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: The guide's average-passenger-car example gives a total stopping distance of two hundred twenty-five feet at fifty-five miles per hour.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: Why does tire condition matter so critically for steering and stopping control?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Tires are the vehicle's only points of contact with the roadway, making their condition important to traction.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: What risk do you trigger by hitting the brakes after entering a curve?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Braking while already inside a curve can trigger a skid.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.front: What actually happens between your tires and the road during hydroplaning?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.expected_back: Hydroplaning occurs when the tires ride on water and lose contact with the road surface.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.front: What prevents hydroplaning in wet weather, and what tire issue raises the danger?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.expected_back: Keeping speed down helps prevent hydroplaning; worn tires increase the risk.

sec11-card-sec11-F40.front: What should your right foot do immediately if your car starts hydroplaning?
sec11-card-sec11-F40.expected_back: If hydroplaning begins, ease your foot off the accelerator gradually.

sec11-card-sec11-F41.front: How should you handle the steering wheel while skimming across standing water?
sec11-card-sec11-F41.expected_back: During hydroplaning, hold the steering straight; if an emergency requires steering, turn slowly.

sec11-card-sec11-F42.front: When is it finally safe to brake or turn after hydroplaning starts?
sec11-card-sec11-F42.expected_back: Wait for tire grip to return before attempting to stop or turn after hydroplaning.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: At what speed does the guide warn tire traction can vanish completely in heavy rain?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: In heavy rain, the guide warns that tire traction may be lost completely at fifty miles per hour.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: How do Arkansas traffic rules treat bicyclists compared with drivers of motor vehicles?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Bicyclists have road rights and responsibilities like other vehicle operators.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: Which side and direction on the roadway should bicycles use relative to motor traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: Bicycles travel with traffic on the road's right-hand side rather than facing approaching traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: Why must drivers expect a cyclist ahead to shift lane position without much warning?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: Expect a bicycle rider to change position suddenly to avoid debris, pavement damage, animals, parked vehicles, or an opening door.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: Why may a bicyclist properly move toward the middle of the lane while riding past parked cars?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: A cyclist passing parked cars may properly move toward the lane center to avoid opening doors or people leaving those cars.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: How much lane space should you give a bicyclist when overtaking, and what if that is impossible?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: Give a bicyclist the full lane when possible; if that cannot be done, pass with extreme caution.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: When you spot a cyclist riding well away from the right curb, what legitimate reasons might explain that position?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: A bicyclist riding away from the right side of the lane is not being careless and may be accounting for traffic conditions or preparing for a left turn.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: What two things must you check carefully before turning across a bicyclist's path of travel?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: Before turning across a bicyclist's route, check carefully for the rider and accurately judge the rider's speed.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: What dangerous right-turn mistake must you never make right after passing a bicyclist?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: Do not overtake a bicyclist and immediately turn right across the rider's path.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: Instead of slicing across a cyclist's line, how should a driver prepare for an upcoming right turn?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: When preparing a right turn, merge with bicycle traffic rather than cutting directly across a cyclist's route.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: What sudden mistake should you anticipate when driving near children on bicycles?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: Watch for children on bicycles who may turn without looking or signaling.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: What visual connection should you try to make with a cyclist before turning near them?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: Try to establish eye contact with a cyclist before turning near that rider.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: How much lateral space should you leave whenever your vehicle overtakes a bicycle?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: Leave ample room when overtaking a bicycle.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: What must you do on a two-lane road when an oncoming car approaches as you catch up to a cyclist?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: On a two-lane road, wait for an approaching vehicle to pass before overtaking a bicycle instead of squeezing between them.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: Under what street conditions must you hold back instead of overtaking a bicyclist?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: Do not pass a cyclist where the road is too narrow or the pass would force the rider dangerously close to parked vehicles.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: How should you use your horn if a cyclist on a narrow road seems unaware that you are approaching?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: If a cyclist on a narrow road appears unaware of your approach, the guide recommends only a brief, gentle horn tap rather than a startling blast.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: Which two traits make motor-vehicle collisions especially dangerous for bicyclists?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: Because bicycles are hard to see and offer no enclosure, riders are exposed and easily injured in a crash.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: What specific visibility danger makes oncoming bicycle traffic risky at intersections?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: Because bicycles are difficult to spot in traffic, oncoming bicycle traffic is frequently overlooked by motorists.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: Where should you scan extra carefully for emerging bicyclists while driving through residential streets?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: In residential areas, watch for bicyclists entering from driveways, behind parked vehicles, or other obstructions.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Why do children on bicycles demand heightened driver alertness compared with adult commuters?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: Children riding bicycles may make sudden movements or changes of direction, requiring extra driver attention.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: What night equipment do bicycles need, and why must drivers stay vigilant anyway?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: At night, bicycles need a front lamp and rear reflector, but drivers must still watch carefully because cyclists are hard to see.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: How much lane space should you grant a bicyclist who is passing another vehicle moving in the same direction?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: Allow a bicyclist the full lane while the rider overtakes another vehicle moving in the same direction.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: Which three maneuvers are prohibited inside a lane marked and signed exclusively for bicycles?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: Do not use a lane marked and signed exclusively for bicycles to turn, pass, or park.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: When a cyclist prepares to turn left at an intersection, private road, or driveway, what lane position is permitted?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: A cyclist preparing a left turn at an intersection, private road, or driveway may use the full lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: What types of unsafe roadway conditions justify a bicyclist taking the full travel lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: Unsafe roadway conditions such as debris, potholes, animals, people, or obstructions can justify a cyclist's full-lane use.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: How should you respond when a traffic lane is too narrow for a car and a bicycle to share side by side safely?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: Let a bicycle take the full lane when the lane is too narrow for a car and bicycle to share safely.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: How do headlights from oncoming traffic affect your ability to see a bicyclist at night?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: Opposing vehicle lights can make an already hard-to-see bicycle less visible at night.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: What does a red or orange pennant on a bicycle indicate in the Arkansas guide, and how should you respond?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: The guide identifies a red or orange pennant on a bicycle as an indication of a rider with impaired hearing and recommends slowing.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: When must you check mirrors and blind spots specifically for motorcycles?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: Before entering or leaving a lane and at intersections, check mirrors and blind spots specifically for motorcycles.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: Why must you give motorcyclists extra room to vary their speed or lane position?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: Leave motorcyclists room to change lane position or speed to avoid hazardous pavement, weather, or traffic conditions.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: What can strong wind or air blasts off a passing large truck do to a motorcycle?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: Strong wind, including gusts from a large truck, can push a motorcycle across a lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: How can vans, buses, or large trucks create a sudden motorcycle surprise in traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: A van, bus, or truck may conceal a motorcycle until the rider emerges into view.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: What extra visual step should you take before turning at an intersection, especially when turning left?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: Take a second look for motorcycles before turning at an intersection, especially before turning left.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: Why is an approaching motorcycle harder to detect in traffic than a passenger car?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: A motorcycle's smaller outline makes it harder to detect than an approaching car.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: Which two motion judgments are harder for motorists to make accurately for a motorcycle than for a car?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: Drivers can have more difficulty judging a motorcycle's distance and speed than a car's.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: Why do skilled motorcyclists frequently shift left or right inside their own traffic lane?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: Motorcycle riders frequently adjust their position within a lane as road conditions change.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: How do minor road flaws like potholes, gravel patches, rail crossings, or slick spots affect motorcycles compared with cars?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: A pothole, gravel patch, rail crossing, or slick surface can pose a much larger hazard to a motorcycle than to a passenger car.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: Which specific intersection maneuver does the Arkansas guide highlight as a common car-motorcycle crash pattern?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: The guide identifies a car's left turn in front of a motorcycle at an intersection as a common car-motorcycle crash pattern.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: When must you signal a lane change or merge to protect possible motorcyclists nearby?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.memory_hook: Signal every move, empty or not
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: Signal every lane change or merge so a motorcyclist can anticipate your movement, even when you see no other vehicle.

sec14-card-sec14-F30.front: How thoroughly should you scan before crossing the path of an approaching motorcycle?
sec14-card-sec14-F30.expected_back: Before crossing an approaching motorcycle's path, look carefully in all directions.

sec14-card-sec14-F31.front: Why must you wait instead of pulling out based solely on a motorcycle's flashing turn signal?
sec14-card-sec14-F31.expected_back: Do not trust a motorcycle's flashing turn signal alone; wait to see whether the rider actually turns.

sec14-card-sec14-F32.front: How much width of a traffic lane belongs to a motorcycle, and may a car drive beside it in that lane?
sec14-card-sec14-F32.expected_back: A motorcycle is entitled to an entire lane; do not attempt to drive alongside it within the same lane.

sec14-card-sec14-F33.front: How many seconds of following space does the Arkansas guide call for when trailing a motorcycle?
sec14-card-sec14-F33.expected_back: When following a motorcycle, the guide calls for additional space of at least four to six seconds.

sec14-card-sec14-F34.front: What can happen to a motorcyclist from even a light tap by another vehicle?
sec14-card-sec14-F34.expected_back: Even slight contact can cause a motorcycle rider to fall or be injured.

sec14-card-sec14-R10.front: Why might a motorcycle keep riding straight even while its turn signal continues flashing?
sec14-card-sec14-R10.expected_back: Motorcycle turn signals do not necessarily cancel themselves, and a rider may forget to switch one off.

sec14-card-sec14-R11.front: On dry pavement, how can a motorcycle's stopping performance compare with a passenger car's?
sec14-card-sec14-R11.expected_back: In dry conditions, a motorcycle may stop more quickly than a passenger car.

sec14-card-sec14-R12.front: How does extra following distance directly help the motorcyclist ahead of you during an emergency?
sec14-card-sec14-R12.expected_back: Extra following space allows a motorcyclist room and time to maneuver or stop in an emergency.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What credential must you hold before driving a motor vehicle on any Arkansas public highway?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Driving on public pavement without proper state authorization turns a routine trip into an unlicensed-driving citation right away.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Once you move to Arkansas and become a resident, how many calendar days do you have to get an Arkansas driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Test questions often mix up thirty-day resident transfers with longer visitor rules, so track your move-in date closely.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.question_text: After how long of physical presence in Arkansas must a nonresident get an Arkansas driver license to keep driving there?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.teaching_text: Even if your permanent home stays elsewhere, half a year inside state borders ends your out-of-state visitor grace period.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.question_text: When can active-duty United States military members or visiting allied foreign service members legally drive in Arkansas on an out-of-state license?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.teaching_text: Military orders excuse switching to an Arkansas card, provided the home credential stays current and the driver meets age sixteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: Under what two conditions may nonresident college or exchange students drive in Arkansas using their home license?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Campus and exchange visitors avoid re-licensing in Arkansas only while their out-of-state card remains unexpired and they are sixteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: What testing break applies to a military spouse whose driver license expired while living outside the United States?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Living overseas on military orders makes state renewals tough, so Arkansas waives retesting under this specific spouse provision.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: What are the minimum ages in Arkansas for a restricted driver license versus a nonrestricted driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Graduated licensing starts early with supervised guardrails at fourteen and unlocks full adult privileges only at age eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: Which three core personal details must every driver license applicant prove with documentation?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Showing up at the testing counter missing proof for any one of those three items stalls your application immediately.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: Whose approval is required before anyone under age eighteen can get an Arkansas driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Until legal adulthood at eighteen, a parent or legal guardian must formally sign off on your driving privilege.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: Which two driving exams appear on the Arkansas driver license eligibility list?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Written rules alone never earn a license because you must also demonstrate safe vehicle control behind the wheel.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: In the license eligibility list, how long past expiration can a hard-copy out-of-state license be and still qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: Bringing a plastic out-of-state card expired past one month means you lose streamlined transfer eligibility at the counter.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: What national residency status appears among the Arkansas driver license eligibility requirements?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: State licensing offices verify lawful presence inside the country before issuing any Arkansas driver credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: How does an unresolved court judgment for a moving traffic violation affect your Arkansas license eligibility?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Leaving an open traffic ticket hanging in court freezes your ability to qualify for a license until resolved.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: Which three court-judged personal conditions disqualify someone under the guide's license eligibility list?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Formal court findings of mental incompetence or severe alcohol or illegal narcotic dependence bar licensing to protect road users.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: Who must sit right beside an Arkansas instruction-permit holder whenever they practice driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Letting an eighteen-year-old friend ride shotgun violates your permit because your front-seat coach must be twenty-one-plus and licensed.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: How old must you be to apply for an Arkansas instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Arkansas lets teens begin supervised road practice early at fourteen so habits solidify long before solo driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: Which two tests must you pass to get an Arkansas instruction permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: You prove you know road law and can see traffic clearly first, saving the road skills exam for later.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: How long is an Arkansas instruction permit valid, and what exact event starts that clock?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: Watch the calendar closely because the two-year window counts from your written exam pass date, not printing day.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: When an instruction-permit holder is driving, which passengers in the vehicle must wear seat belts?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: While adults usually focus on front-seat rules, a permit driver is responsible for making sure back-seat riders buckle too.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: Which applicant age bracket qualifies for the restricted learner license in Arkansas?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Know the exact graduated ladder so you never confuse the fourteen-to-sixteen learner stage with sixteen-to-eighteen intermediate cards.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: What three completed exams must appear on your instruction permit before you can get a learner license?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Upgrading from a practice permit to a learner license requires passing the behind-the-wheel road test in addition to earlier exams.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: Which two milestones must both be reached before learner-license driving restrictions lift?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Turning sixteen alone does not end supervision if you have not also logged the full six months of restricted driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: What supervision and seat-belt rules apply whenever someone drives on a learner license?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Even after passing the road exam at fourteen or fifteen, a learner driver still needs twenty-one-plus supervision and full cabin belts.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: When is a learner-license driver allowed to talk or text on a cell phone behind the wheel?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Hands-free Bluetooth does not save a learner driver from a ticket because any non-emergency phone talk or text is banned.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: What crash and violation record must an applicant maintain over the prior six months to qualify for a learner license?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Any recent crash or serious moving conviction resets your clean-record window and delays advancing in the graduated system.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Which age group does the Arkansas intermediate driver license cover?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: Sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds sit in this middle tier where solo driving begins under passenger, phone, and late-night limits.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: Which completed tests must be recorded on an applicant's instruction permit to obtain an intermediate license?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Whether entering at fourteen or sixteen, every teen license tier requires documented proof of all three state exams.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: While an intermediate license still has its supervision restriction active, who must ride along and who must wear seat belts?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Skipping the learner stage at sixteen still leaves an initial restricted period where adult supervision and every-seat belts remain mandatory.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: Where on an Arkansas intermediate license can you check the exact dates when its driving restrictions apply?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Officers and teen drivers flip the plastic license over to verify the exact date when supervision limits expire.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: When may a driver holding a restricted intermediate license talk or text on a cell phone?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Phone chatter splits attention fast for newly licensed teens, so both calls and texts stay off-limits outside genuine emergencies.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: Under what condition may an intermediate-license driver carry more than one unrelated minor passenger?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Packing friends into a car spikes teen crash rates, so carrying two or more unrelated minors requires a licensed twenty-one-plus front passenger.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: During which overnight hours is intermediate-license driving restricted, and what exceptions allow driving then?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Late-night fatigue and low visibility peak between eleven at night and four in the morning unless an approved trip or twenty-one-plus companion applies.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: At what age can an eligible driver receive a nonrestricted Arkansas Class D license?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Reaching eighteen clears teen passenger and curfew limits once you qualify for the standard adult passenger credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: What completed testing must a valid instruction permit show before you can receive a Class D license?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Adult first-time applicants follow the exact same three-exam verification trail on their permit before claiming a full license.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: After finishing all Class D testing requirements, which state office issues your physical driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: State police examiners score your tests, while the Arkansas Revenue Office handles final credential issuance and fee processing.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: What type of wireless phone communication is legal for a Class D driver aged eighteen through twenty?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Turning eighteen unlocks hands-free voice calls on Bluetooth or speaker, though holding the phone in your hand stays restricted.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: When may a Class D driver aged eighteen, nineteen, or twenty use a handheld wireless phone behind the wheel?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Drivers under twenty-one still face a ticket for holding a phone to their ear during routine traffic unless calling for urgent help.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.question_text: At what age does it become legal to send text messages while driving in Arkansas?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.teaching_text: Watch out for trick answers suggesting twenty-one unlocks texting, because typing messages behind the wheel is illegal for every driver.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: Up to what gross vehicle weight do Arkansas noncommercial permits, teen licenses, and Class D licenses cover?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Once a four-wheel truck hits twenty-six thousand one pounds or higher, standard passenger credentials no longer cover the rig.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: Starting at what designed passenger count does a vehicle require a commercial driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Driving a large shuttle or church bus built for sixteen or more riders crosses out of Class D territory into commercial rules.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: What type of cargo requires the driver to hold a commercial driver license regardless of passenger count?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Hauling regulated hazardous cargo demands specialized commercial training and endorsements to prevent catastrophic highway spills.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: When must an applicant pass a vision test in the Arkansas licensing process?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Every driver must prove safe eyesight upfront before receiving either a first instruction permit or an Arkansas driver license.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: What uncorrected visual acuity score is needed to get an unrestricted Arkansas license without corrective lenses?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Meeting twenty over forty with your natural eyesight lets you drive legally without an eyewear code printed on your card.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: What minimum corrected visual acuity qualifies an applicant for a restricted license requiring glasses or contacts while driving?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: If glasses or contacts bring your sight to at least twenty over seventy, you can drive provided you wear them every trip.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How wide must your side-to-side field of vision measure if you have two functioning eyes?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Peripheral sight spots cross-traffic, cyclists, and merging cars long before you turn your head at intersections.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: What minimum field of vision is required for an Arkansas applicant who has one functioning eye?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Exam questions pair one hundred forty degrees for two eyes against one hundred five degrees for monocular drivers, so keep both sharp.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How long do an Arkansas vision test result and a completed vision referral form stay valid?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Waiting longer than twelve months after your eye exam forces you to retest before the state will issue your card.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: Who is required to fill out an Arkansas vision referral form?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Only an in-state optometrist's signature satisfies the referral requirement when counter screening sends you for a deeper eye check.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: Which two kinds of optometrist vision referral forms will Arkansas refuse to accept?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Booking a telehealth eye check or visiting an optometrist across the state border wastes money because examiners reject both forms.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.question_text: Which state agency handles applicant questions and assistance for reciprocal testing exemptions in Arkansas?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.teaching_text: Knowing which agency manages reciprocal license rules saves a wasted trip when transferring foreign or specialized credentials.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Which two groups face temporary hazards during highway construction and maintenance?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Work-zone crashes frequently injure vehicle occupants right alongside crews standing feet from live highway lanes.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: What two everyday driving rules often tighten up inside a highway work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Narrowed shoulders, concrete barriers, and active crews leave less margin for speed or last-second lane weaving.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: Which speed limit governs a work zone when no reduced speed sign is posted?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Never invent your own highway crawl or speed past the regular limit when orange signs carry no temporary number.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: How long can a standard highway construction work zone remain in one place?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: Even if you drive a long-term project every morning, lane shifts and worker locations can change overnight.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: How does a mobile work zone behave compared with a stationary construction site?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Rolling maintenance trucks surprise fast highway drivers because the work area moves down the road instead of staying put.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: Which three road-maintenance jobs does the guide name as common examples of mobile work zones?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Paint trucks, debris sweeps, and patching crews roll forward constantly without miles of orange barrels ahead of them.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: What do flashing green lights on an Arkansas construction or maintenance vehicle mean, and how should you respond?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Arkansas added high-visibility green beacons to maintenance rigs so drivers spot active crews earlier and ease off the gas.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: Which two other warning-light colors can authorized green construction-vehicle lights pair with?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Combining green flashes with familiar amber or white strobes cuts through bright afternoon glare and nighttime headlights alike.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: Which sign shapes and background colors can warn or guide you inside a work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: While bright orange diamonds dominate temporary warnings, white or black rectangles also post enforceable speed and lane rules.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: Which four temporary road conditions can work-zone warning signs alert you to ahead?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Reading temporary legends early keeps grooved asphalt, heavy dump trucks, or sharp detours from catching your tires off guard.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: What is a flagger's job in a highway work area, and what tools do they hold?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Treat a worker holding a paddle or bright flag like a live traffic signal protecting crews around blind equipment.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: From two thousand eighteen to two thousand twenty-one, by how much did Arkansas work-zone crashes climb?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: That steep four-year surge explains why Arkansas tightened work-zone enforcement, camera monitoring, and doubled fines.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: How many Arkansas work-zone crashes and serious injuries or deaths does the guide report for two thousand twenty-four?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: More than sixteen hundred crashes in a single year show how fast tailgating or glancing down turns construction lanes dangerous.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: From two thousand sixteen through two thousand twenty, what percentages of Arkansas traffic deaths and serious injuries came from speeding and aggressive driving?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Nearly one in four roadway deaths traced straight back to rushing and aggressive moves that erase stopping distance.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: How many people died nationwide in distracted-driving crashes during two thousand twenty-three according to the guide?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Thousands of preventable deaths in one year underscore why phones and dash screens never belong in active traffic.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: According to national research cited in the guide, how much more likely are texting teens to crash?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Looking down to read or type pulls eyes, hands, and mind off the lane simultaneously, multiplying teen crash odds twenty-three-fold.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Why do distracted-driving crashes often cause worse injuries than other collisions?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: An attentive driver usually scrubs off speed before impact, whereas a distracted driver often hits stopped traffic at full highway pace.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: What specific condition inside a work zone doubles the normal fine for a moving traffic violation?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Watch exam wording carefully because Arkansas ties doubled work-zone moving-violation fines specifically to workers being present.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: Which types of work zones carry doubled moving-violation fines when workers are present?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Passing a slow striping truck recklessly costs double just like speeding past long-term interstate concrete barriers with crews out.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: Which three broad examples of moving violations trigger the work-zone double-fine rule?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Doubled penalties reach beyond radar tickets to include aggressive lane cutting and phone distraction around active crews.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.question_text: Which four handheld phone habits count as distracted-driving moving violations inside an Arkansas work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.teaching_text: Tapping GPS directions or scrolling feeds in hand counts as a moving violation in construction lanes just like dialing or texting.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: What must you do with your phone inside a work zone if your car has no hands-free setup?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Lacking Bluetooth never excuses holding a phone near cones and crews, so let calls go to voicemail until clear.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: When should you start slowing down for a work zone, and when may you speed back up?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Accelerating as soon as you pass the last worker risks a ticket if you have not yet passed a new speed sign.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: What two smart route habits should you practice before heading out on a trip that may cross work zones?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Spotting construction backups before leaving home lets you detour cleanly without rushing late through narrow cone chutes.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: What two quick cabin adjustments cut distractions right before you enter a work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Quieting cabin audio and stashing your screen frees your eyes and ears for sudden brake lights, backup alarms, and flaggers.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: How early does the Arkansas guide recommend merging into the open lane ahead of a work-zone lane closure?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Racing to the nose of the arrow board triggers hard braking waves and side-swipe collisions right beside barriers.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: What two sudden traffic slowdowns must you always expect when approaching road construction?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Freeway traffic can drop from seventy to zero around one curve when dump trucks enter or lanes pinch down.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: Which five hazards and guide markers should you actively scan for inside an active work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Temporary lane lines weave around workers and heavy equipment, so scanning ahead keeps you centered between barrels.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: Why is keeping generous following space behind the car ahead critical inside a work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Tailgating between concrete barriers leaves nowhere to swerve when the line of cars ahead slams on the brakes.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: Which four work-zone warnings and traffic controls must every driver obey?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Channeling cones and flagger paddles carry enforceable legal weight to keep cars out of open trenches and crew zones.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: Up to how many dollars can doubled work-zone fines climb in Arkansas when workers are present?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Serious moving offenses around active highway crews can carry staggering four-figure fines once the double-penalty statute kicks in.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: Where are the warning signs mounted that identify an active mobile work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Because rolling crews do not plant roadside signposts every hundred yards, the tailgates of highway trucks carry the warnings.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: Where can an officer wait while monitoring an interstate work-zone speed camera in Arkansas?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Camera enforcement catches speeders mid-project while the trooper waits at the exit end ready to pull violators over.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: How does interstate work-zone camera enforcement keep police officers safer?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Pulling speeders over after the barrels clear avoids squeezing patrol cars and troopers into shoulderless construction chutes.

sec03-card-sec03-R11.question_text: What advance signs and three flashing light colors can mark a mobile work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-R11.teaching_text: Spotting a work-ahead placard followed by green, amber, or white flashes tells you slow-moving maintenance trucks sit ahead.

sec03-card-sec03-R12.question_text: How far through a construction project should you continue watching and following work-zone signs?
sec03-card-sec03-R12.teaching_text: Secondary crews and lane merges often sit near the tail end of a project long after the main paving machines.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: Which lane should you move into when approaching a stationary roadside response or work vehicle?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Vacating the lane right beside a stopped rig creates a full lane width of breathing room for workers stepping out.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: What must you do when traffic or road width makes changing lanes away from a stopped roadside vehicle unsafe or impossible?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: Never force a sideswipe into heavy traffic; instead drop your speed right away to a safe or legally required pace.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: Which four types of non-police work vehicles with flashing lights receive protection under Arkansas's move-over rule?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Arkansas extends move-over protection beyond squad cars and ambulances to every flashing highway, utility, construction, and tow crew.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: Who wins if a work-zone flagger's paddle or hand signal conflicts with a posted sign or traffic signal?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Flaggers see live equipment swings and one-lane queues that fixed signs and automated lights cannot detect.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: Where must you stop for a work-zone flagger if no specific spot is pointed out, and when may you roll?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Stopping at least a full car length back gives the flagger visibility and escape room until they wave you forward.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: How should you position your vehicle around work-zone workers and heavy machinery?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: Excavators swing counterweights and workers carry tools, so crowding the cone line leaves zero margin for human movement.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: Which four roadway changes and obstacles should you stay ready for inside a work zone?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Milled pavement edges, sudden jogs across lanes, lower limits, and slow haul trucks demand two hands and calm steering.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: How can a two-way road keep moving when construction closes one lane, and who may lead traffic through?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Patience is vital on one-lane closures because pulling out before the flagger or pilot car turns around causes head-on conflicts.

sec03-card-sec03-R13.question_text: What real-world safety goal do move-over laws accomplish beside the highway?
sec03-card-sec03-R13.teaching_text: One distracted drift over the fog line can be fatal unless passing cars leave an empty buffer lane.

sec03-card-sec03-R14.question_text: Which four legal penalties can hit a driver convicted of violating Arkansas move-over laws?
sec03-card-sec03-R14.teaching_text: Skipping a simple lane change can cost far more than cash, putting both your freedom and driver license at risk.

sec03-card-sec03-R15.question_text: Do work-zone flaggers hold actual legal authority to control traffic, or are their signals only advisory?
sec03-card-sec03-R15.teaching_text: Ignoring a flagger carries moving-violation consequences because state law empowers them to control temporary traffic patterns.

sec03-card-sec03-R16.question_text: Which four tools and cues do work-zone flaggers use to communicate with approaching drivers?
sec03-card-sec03-R16.teaching_text: Recognizing octagonal stop-or-slow paddles, bright flags, and hand signals right away prevents hesitation at one-lane work zones.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: Which roadway devices and authorized people make up traffic control in Arkansas?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Traffic control spans overhead lights, roadside signs, painted lines, and live human directions from officers, crews, and school guards.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: Are roadway traffic controls optional suggestions or mandatory rules for Arkansas drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Every intersection depends on shared predictability, so ignoring a sign, line, or signal breaks right-of-way expectations immediately.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: Even when your traffic signal is green, what must happen before you enter the intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: A green bulb grants permission to go only after turning cars and pedestrians already in your path finish clearing.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: When waiting stopped at a red light that turns green, who must you let clear before accelerating?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Jackrabbit starts on a fresh green cause T-bone crashes against late cross-traffic or left-turners still clearing the box.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: What must you do at a steady red traffic light if you plan to go straight through?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: While turns on red have narrow exceptions, straight-through traffic must always hold a complete stop until green appears safely.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: What signal phase change does a steady yellow traffic light warn you is happening?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Treating yellow as a speed-up challenge puts you into the intersection right as cross-traffic gets a green light.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What is the right move when a traffic light turns steady yellow ahead of you?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Smoothly braking to a stop whenever distance allows keeps you out of red-light tickets and late-phase intersection crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: If you are already stopped at an intersection or stop line when a yellow light shows, may you pull forward?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Rolling out from a stop during a yellow clearance phase puts you directly in front of oncoming red-phase traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: Which common roadside sign matches the exact rule for a flashing red traffic light?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Never confuse flashing red with flashing yellow because flashing red demands a dead stop before checking cross-traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: How should you drive through an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow traffic signal?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Slamming to a surprise stop under a flashing yellow invites rear-end hits, whereas easing off the gas keeps scanning sharp.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: Which three colors make up standard Arkansas traffic signals?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Standardized color order and shades help drivers recognize stop, caution, and go phases instantly in glare or rain.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: What movement does a steady red directional arrow forbid?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Watch out for the right-on-red habit because a steady red arrow blocks turning in its pointed direction completely.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: What does a steady yellow turn arrow warn of, and how should a left-turning driver respond?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Protected turn time is expiring, so braking smoothly keeps you from getting stranded across oncoming lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: Who must you yield to before turning left on a flashing yellow arrow?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Oncoming straight traffic holds a green light during your flashing yellow arrow, so misjudging their speed causes severe front-angle crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: Why is a turn made on a green directional arrow called a protected turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: While opposing cars face a red signal during your green arrow, still scan for red-light runners and crosswalk stragglers.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: When you sit in a dedicated turn lane governed by its own signal arrow, when should you make your turn?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Do not jump on the adjacent straight-lane green ball when your dedicated turn bay has its own arrow head.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: How do right-of-way rules differ on a green left arrow compared with a flashing yellow left arrow?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Exam questions love contrasting protected green arrows against permissive flashing yellow arrows where oncoming traffic and walkers go first.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: Before turning right at a steady red light, what two things must you do first?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Rolling through a right on red without a dead stop is one of the top automatic-fail mistakes on road tests.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: Even after a full stop and clear check, what posted condition makes a right turn on red illegal?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Always scan beside the signal head and corner post for a no-turn-on-red plaque before creeping into a turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: How must you handle crosswalks and people on foot before turning right on red?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Drivers staring left for gaps in cars often miss pedestrians stepping off the right curb right beside their hood.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: Which unique side count and color combination identify a standard stop sign?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Giving the octagon solely to stop signs lets you recognize a required stop even from behind or coated in frost.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: What two steps are required at every stop sign before you pull into the intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: Wheels must stop turning completely before you wait out crossing pedestrians and vehicles holding the right-of-way.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: When a stop-controlled intersection has a painted white stopping line, where do you bring your car to a halt?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Rolling past the white bar noses your bumper into the crosswalk or turning path of wide trucks.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: How should you handle a stop sign when parked cars, hedges, or buildings block your view of cross-traffic?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Skipping the first legal stop to nose out for a view fails road exams and surprises pedestrians on the sidewalk.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: What road conditions are posted maximum speed limits designed for, and what must you do in slick or foggy weather?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: You can still get cited and hydroplane below the posted number if rain, ice, or fog cuts traction and sight.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: What does a yield sign require you to do as you enter or cross an intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Treat a yield sign as a conditional stop whenever cross-traffic is close enough to create any conflict.
sec04-card-sec04-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Yield intersection traffic, stop if needed

visual_sync.text_span: Yield intersection traffic, stop if needed

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: What shape, center color, and border color make up a slow-moving-vehicle emblem?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: Daytime fluorescent orange and nighttime red reflectors help highway drivers spot farm tractors and buggies from far back.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: What does seeing an orange-and-red triangle mounted on the back of a vehicle ahead tell you?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: At highway speed you close the gap on a tractor in seconds, so lift off the gas immediately upon spotting the triangle.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: What shape, background color, and print color do most permanent road warning signs use?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Spotting a yellow diamond far ahead primes you for curves, merges, or crossings before you can even read the symbol.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: What do road warning signs alert you to, and what speed adjustments might they require?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: Warning signs give advance notice of hidden curves, crossings, or slick spots so you never brake late inside the hazard.
sec04-card-sec04-F28.must_match_memory_hook: Road hazards ahead, slow or stop

visual_sync.text_span: Road hazards ahead, slow or stop

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: Which four everyday driving rules do regulatory signs commonly govern?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Unlike advisory yellow warnings, regulatory signs post enforceable traffic laws that carry citations if disobeyed.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: Which five kinds of helpful roadway information can traffic signs give drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Road signs combine legal rules and hazard alerts with practical route guidance toward towns, exits, fuel, and hospitals.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: Why do highway engineers standardize sign shapes and background colors?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: Instant visual coding lets your brain separate a regulatory law from a hazard warning or exit guide in a split second.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: Which two kinds of legal speed boundaries can speed-limit signs post for a stretch of road?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: High-speed highways sometimes post minimum speeds alongside maximums so dangerously slow vehicles do not trigger rear-end crashes.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: Which three major roadway types are excluded from Arkansas's definition of a county road?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Knowing where county jurisdiction stops helps you apply the right rural speed rules outside cities and state highways.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: Which local official has authority to set speed limits on county roads in Arkansas?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Arkansas places county-road speed authority with the county judge rather than city councils or neighborhood groups.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: What default speed limit applies on an Arkansas county road when the county judge has not set another limit?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: Unmarked rural county roads often wind past blind hills, gravel driveways, and farm equipment where higher speeds turn deadly.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: Going how many miles per hour above a posted Arkansas county-road limit becomes a Class C misdemeanor?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Pushing past fifteen miles per hour over a posted county limit escalates your ticket into a Class C misdemeanor.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.question_text: Which statewide manual must traffic-control devices on Arkansas county roads follow?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.teaching_text: Requiring one uniform manual across every county stops confusing homemade signs and keeps shapes and colors consistent statewide.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.question_text: What maximum fine and license-suspension length does the guide list for failing to yield?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.teaching_text: Cutting off right-of-way can cost up to a thousand dollars and park your driver license for roughly six months.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.question_text: What shape and two possible color combinations does the Arkansas guide describe for yield signs?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.teaching_text: While modern yield signs shine red and white, the Arkansas manual still tests recognition of older yellow-and-black triangles too.

sec04-card-sec04-R13.question_text: What shape, background color, and print colors are standard on most regulatory signs?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.teaching_text: Vertical white rectangles post speed limits and lane laws clearly, often adding red circles or slashes for prohibitions.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.question_text: Which seven common road hazards and crossings appear in the guide's warning-sign examples?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.teaching_text: Knowing the core symbol family lets you spot upcoming signals, slippery pavement, lane drops, schools, and crosswalks instantly.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: How must you respond to railroad crossing warnings, barriers, and an oncoming train?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Trying to beat a locomotive or weave past a lowered arm turns an ordinary delay into a fatal collision.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: How much room do you need past the rails before driving onto a railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Entering tracks while traffic ahead is backed up can trap your rear bumper directly in a locomotive path.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: Why must drivers of manual-transmission vehicles avoid shifting gears while crossing railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Missing a shift mid-crossing can stall the engine and leave your car stranded right across active rails.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: What shape and colors identify the advance warning marker placed ahead of a public highway-rail crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Spotting the circular yellow warning early gives you crucial distance to ease off the gas before reaching the rails.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: What three actions should you take as soon as you reach an advance railroad warning?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Easing speed while scanning and listening early ensures you can brake smoothly instead of skidding toward the rails.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: Which painted letters, symbol, and two-lane passing line warn drivers of railroad tracks ahead?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Roadway paint reinforces roadside posts when foliage or large trucks block your view of vertical crossing markers.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: What painted line may mark the stopping point on the approach side of railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Halting behind the painted white stripe keeps your front bumper safely clear of overhanging freight cars and lowering arms.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: What shape, color, and placement identify a railroad crossbuck?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Recognizing the white X-shaped post right at the rails tells you immediately where the track hazard zone sits.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: Who gets the right of way whenever a railroad crossbuck stands at a crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Freight trains need massive braking distances and cannot swerve, making a crossbuck function just like a yield command.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: What action is mandatory for school buses when they arrive at railroad crossings?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Trailing behind a yellow bus near tracks without leaving braking margin risks rear-ending a vehicle required to halt.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: How does the message of railroad pavement paint compare with the round advance warning marker?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Pairing painted lane markings with the circular roadside post gives drivers two redundant alerts before reaching active rails.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: What extra overtaking restriction marker may stand along a two-lane approach to railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Pulling into the oncoming lane near tracks invites a collision with hidden cars or stopped vehicles waiting for trains.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: Are you ever allowed to steer around a lowered railroad crossing gate?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Zigzagging past a down arm puts your car directly into the path of a fast-moving train you misjudged.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: May you drive across railroad tracks while red lights flash if you see no train coming?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Curves, brush, or a passing freight car can hide an oncoming locomotive while red warning lamps are active.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: What event is being announced when crossing lights start flashing and gates start coming down?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Treating descending arms as an early yellow light to beat ignores the fast-closing locomotive triggering the track sensors.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: What legal and safety status applies to the roadway once a railroad crossing gate is lowered?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Crossing past a lowered barrier breaks Arkansas traffic law and gambles your life against thousands of tons of steel.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: What should you do if a crossing gate starts coming down after you have already entered the tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Stopping or reversing traps your car on the rails, whereas fiberglass gate arms are built to snap cleanly.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: What visual check is required before crossing railroad tracks that have no safety barrier?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Without automated gates to block your lane, your own two-way scan is the sole defense against an unannounced train.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Whose contact details are posted on the emergency-notification plaque at a railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Calling the rail operator directly lets dispatchers halt oncoming locomotives faster when a vehicle stalls across the rails.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Why does an emergency-notification plaque list an identifier for that exact railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Giving dispatchers the exact crossing code lets them stop trains on the right rail line without losing precious seconds.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: How do the red warning lights mounted next to some railroad crossbucks operate?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: Alternating red beams grab peripheral vision far quicker than a steady bulb when a train triggers the circuit.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: Where is the black-on-yellow EXEMPT railroad plaque mounted according to the Arkansas guide?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Written questions test color-and-post pairings closely, matching the yellow exempt panel with the yellow advance warning post.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: Where does the black-on-white EXEMPT railroad plaque appear at a crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Matching background colors keeps the pair straight, since white exempt lettering hangs right beneath the white crossbuck.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: What hidden danger must you watch for at a crossing with more than one railroad track?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Pulling out right behind a departing caboose blinds you to a second locomotive barreling down the adjacent rail.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: What does a numbered plaque mounted directly beneath a railroad crossbuck tell you?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Knowing exact track count warns you before moving forward that more than one train path crosses your lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: When is it safe to start driving across a multiple-track crossing after a train clears your lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Waiting until the first train travels well down the line restores a clear view of every parallel track.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: Are you ever permitted to stop or park a vehicle on railroad tracks?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Idling or parking across steel rails leaves zero escape time if a high-speed train rounds the bend.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Where must you look every single time your vehicle approaches a railroad crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Warning bells or lights can malfunction during storms, so scanning down both rail directions remains mandatory every trip.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: How should you treat a railroad crossing where you have never seen a train before?
