sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Freight schedules shift without public notice, turning a seemingly unused spur into an active line when least expected.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: What mistake must you avoid when judging an approaching train's speed and distance?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Large objects create an optical illusion of slow motion, making locomotives close the gap far quicker than expected.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: What train possibility do multiple-track warning plaques alert drivers to expect?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Parallel rails carry two-way rail traffic simultaneously, meaning two locomotives can reach the same crossing seconds apart.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: Does one train finishing its pass prove that every other track at the crossing is clear?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Assuming adjacent rails are empty right after one train clears causes classic second-train collisions at multi-track junctions.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: Do railroad crossing warnings still have to be obeyed on routes you drive every day?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Daily routine breeds complacency, yet trains strike local commuters on neighborhood crossings just as hard as strangers.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: What do right-of-way laws actually define instead of giving anyone an unconditional right to drive ahead?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Treating right-of-way as a green light to charge forward causes T-bone wrecks whenever another motorist makes a mistake.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: What duty stays on every driver even when traffic rules say another person should yield?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Winning a legal argument means nothing in a collision, so preventing contact overrides right-of-way status every single time.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: How must you respond whenever yielding is needed to avoid striking a pedestrian crossing legally?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Steel beats flesh every time, requiring drivers to brake and yield whenever someone is lawfully crossing the roadway.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: Who holds priority when your car crosses a sidewalk to enter or exit a driveway, alley, or lot?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Joggers and families on sidewalks often miss quiet cars nosing out between buildings or parked SUVs.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: What is the lone legal movement a motor vehicle may make across a sidewalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Using a walkway to bypass street congestion is illegal because pedestrians never expect moving traffic along the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Which pedestrians receive unconditional, absolute right of way on Arkansas streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Visually impaired walkers navigate by sound and timing, so every approaching driver must yield completely without hesitation.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: Why must you keep off your horn near a blind pedestrian?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: A sudden blast drowns out directional street audio that visually impaired pedestrians rely on to stay safe.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: Which oncoming traffic must you yield to before turning left across an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Misjudging the closing speed of an oncoming car going straight causes some of the severest intersection angle crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: What decides which vehicle waits when an intersection has neither traffic lights nor control posts?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Quiet neighborhood four-ways lack hardware, yet statutory priority rules still govern every approach so cars never guess.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: How does the left-turn yield rule separate the roles of two oncoming drivers at an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Because the left turner cuts directly across the opposing lane, the driver holding a straight line keeps priority.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: Who gets priority when your vehicle approaches the entrance of a traffic circle or rotary?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Forcing your nose into an active rotary disrupts circular flow and triggers immediate side-angle impacts.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: How does the Arkansas guide describe the layout and flow of a roundabout?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Channeling every approach around a raised center island eliminates high-speed ninety-degree T-bone conflict points.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: Which approaching vehicle gets priority at an intersection with no stop posts or traffic signals?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Checking right and yielding at open residential corners stops simultaneous arrivals from colliding in the middle.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: Which vehicle goes ahead of yours when stop posts control every approach to an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Tracking arrival order as you roll up keeps multi-way stops orderly and prevents awkward bumper-inching standoffs.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: How does the first driver to reach a three-way, four-way, or all-way stop earn the turn to go?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Arriving earliest never excuses a rolling California stop, because your wheels must cease motion before claiming priority.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: Which three practical benefits does the Arkansas guide highlight for circular roundabouts?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Eliminating overhead signal wiring cuts upkeep costs while keeping cars moving smoothly at safer low speeds.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: How does priority at an all-stop corner differ from priority at an uncontrolled intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Written exams love mixing up arrival-order stops with open residential corners where right-side position breaks conflicts.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: What mandatory step must happen before a first-arriving driver uses priority at an all-way stop?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Coasting through first because nobody else stopped yet violates stop-control law and invites cross-traffic collisions.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: Who must yield when a car pulls onto a street from a driveway, alley, or roadside shoulder?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Through traffic moves at full roadway speed, so pulling out from private access without a big gap causes rear-ends.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: When are you allowed to drive into an intersection if traffic ahead is backed up?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Creeping forward on green without room past the crosswalk strands your car sideways across perpendicular traffic once lights flip.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: Which directions must you scan before pulling into any intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Red-light runners and fast bicycles can arrive from either cross-street side even after your own light turns green.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: What duty toward the vehicle ahead remains yours while overtaking in the same direction, even if it slows?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Blaming a slowing lead car while swinging past ignores your legal duty to clear its path safely.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: What should you do when congestion ahead could trap your car inside an intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Holding back behind the stop bar keeps cross streets open for emergency rigs and perpendicular green phases.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: What unseen reasons might cause a vehicle ahead of you to slow down right as you plan to pass?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Whipping around a braking car can put you broadside into its left turn or straight into a crossing pedestrian.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: What sudden actions should you watch for from the vehicle you are overtaking?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Keeping eyes on front tires and brake lamps while passing gives early warning before an unsignaled turn cuts left.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: What two qualities make a parking spot safe for approaching traffic in both directions?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Tucking a car just past a blind crest or curve turns a parked bumper into a sudden obstacle.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: How must you check for walkers and cars before reversing straight or backing out of a parking spot?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Mirrors leave wide rear blind zones where small children or shopping carts disappear unless you turn your head.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Where should you park whenever a marked, designated parking area is available?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Choosing off-street stalls instead of improvised roadside shoulders keeps your doors and mirrors safely away from fast traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: What two steps secure manual and automatic vehicles once you finish parking?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Relying on transmission pawls or engine compression alone risks a runaway rollaway if the holding mechanism slips.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: What safety habit applies before swinging open a door and stepping out of a parked car?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Flinging a street-side door into an oncoming cyclist or passing mirror causes severe injuries that a curb exit prevents.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: What is the maximum distance allowed between your tires and the curb when parallel parking?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Leaving a wider gap sticks your street-side quarter panel out into the active travel lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: How should you position your vehicle along a roadside where parking is legal?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Maximizing separation from moving lanes gives passing trucks extra buffer room past your side mirrors.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: What two actions are required before walking away from a vehicle parked on a noticeable slope?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Angling front tires properly lets the curb or shoulder catch the car harmlessly if brakes ever slip.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: What must you do first when exiting from the traffic side of your parked vehicle cannot be avoided?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Waiting two seconds for a clear gap behind your mirror prevents passing traffic from ripping your door off.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: What overall safety standard governs every spot where you leave a stationary vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Even without a no-parking post nearby, leaving a car where it endangers flowing traffic remains unlawful.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: Are you ever allowed to park a vehicle inside an intersection?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: A stationary car inside corner sightlines blinds turning drivers and chokes cross-street traffic movement.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: How close to an intersection crosswalk are you prohibited from parking?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Parking right against the painted stripes hides stepping pedestrians behind your hood until approaching cars are too close.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: What minimum distance must a parked car keep from a stop sign, yield sign, or traffic signal?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Tall SUVs or vans parked closer than thirty feet block approaching drivers from spotting stop or yield commands.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: How far away must you park from a pedestrian safety zone?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Keeping thirty feet clear preserves open sightlines around transit islands and protected pedestrian refuge areas.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: Within what distance of a fire hydrant is parking strictly prohibited?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Fire crews need fifteen unobstructed feet at the curb to swing heavy supply hoses onto hydrant valves fast.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: How far back from a railroad crossing must all parked vehicles remain?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Parking closer than fifty feet blocks driver views down the rails and obscures flashing crossing signals.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: Which curb cuts and property entrances must never be blocked by a parked vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Blocking alleys, private lanes, or lowered sidewalk ramps traps residents inside and cuts off wheelchair curb access.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: How close to a same-side fire-station driveway does the Arkansas guide ban parking?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Wide ladder trucks need generous curb swing clearance to pull out rapidly onto emergency response calls.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: What distance from the curb puts a parked car in violation of Arkansas parking rules?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Examiners flip the eighteen-inch rule both ways, testing whether anything past eighteen inches triggers a ticket.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: When does parking across a crosswalk or sidewalk in a construction zone violate the guide's rules?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Work zones already narrow lanes and detours, so obstructing temporary walkways forces people out into active machinery.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What parking rule applies on bridges, overpasses, tunnels, and underpasses?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Elevated decks and enclosed bores have zero shoulder escape room, turning any parked car into a bottleneck hazard.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: May you park along a street facing against the flow of traffic in that lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Parking nose-first on the left curb forces you to cross oncoming traffic blindly both arriving and pulling out.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: What credential is legally required before parking in an accessible disability stall?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Borrowing an accessible stall without a valid disability credential steals essential ramp space and triggers steep fines.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: Are you allowed to double-park in the street alongside another car already parked at the curb?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Stopping side-by-side in an active travel lane traps the curb car inside and forces flowing traffic across centerlines.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: May an unattended or parked vehicle ever be left sitting on railroad tracks?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Locomotives cannot steer around or stop short of an abandoned car sitting across active steel rails.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: What rule applies throughout any curb stretch marked by a posted no-parking sign?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Posted curb bans protect tight truck turns, bus stops, or sightlines even when the asphalt looks wide open.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: What restricted area does a red-painted curb identify?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Emergency pumpers and ambulances need red-curb frontage completely open so crews reach building entrances immediately.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: What does a yellow-painted curb tell drivers looking for a place to park?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Treating yellow curb paint like open all-day parking risks a tow from commercial delivery or restricted spaces.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Which two roadside indicators should you check before claiming any curb parking spot?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Checking solely at eye height misses painted curb bans, while looking solely down misses time-restricted roadside posts.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: When must you fasten your safety belt and verify its fit?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Fumbling with belt straps after rolling steals eyes and hands from driveways and parking aisles.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Across which part of your body must the shoulder belt sit—and where must it never go?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Routing the strap across your collarbone and sternum lets strong rib-cage bones absorb forward crash energy.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: What happens to your crash protection if you tuck the diagonal shoulder strap behind your back?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Without torso restraint, your upper body whips violently into the steering wheel or dashboard on impact.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: Where must the lap belt rest rather than across your stomach, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Strong pelvic hip bones handle crash deceleration, whereas a high belt across soft abdominal organs causes severe internal trauma.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: How should you sit in the driver's seat so your safety belt lines up properly?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Slouching slides your hips forward under the lap strap so crash forces hit soft organs instead of bone.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: What two goals guide adjusting your driver's seat distance and height?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Balancing relaxed arm-and-pedal reach with clear sightlines out every window prevents blind spots and fatigue.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: Why must both lap and shoulder straps lie flat against your body without twists?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Twisted belt webbing narrows into a rope-like edge that concentrates painful crash force along one narrow strip.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: What quick physical check confirms your seat-belt buckle actually locked?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Coins, crumbs, or winter coat fabric inside a buckle housing can fake a click without locking the tongue.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Does studying the Arkansas driver's manual replace behind-the-wheel instruction and practice?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Knowing right-of-way rules on paper still needs coached seat time to build smooth muscle-memory reactions.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How do safety belts distribute impact forces across the human frame?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Distributing stopping loads across wide chest and hip bones prevents single-point concentrated trauma.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: How should you press the accelerator pedal when pulling away or building speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Feeding throttle smoothly keeps weight balanced over all four tires and saves fuel.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: What traction trouble can punching the gas abruptly trigger, especially on wet asphalt?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Wet pavement slashes tire friction, letting sudden torque spin drive wheels sideways before you clear the line.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: Which two pedals must a manual-transmission driver practice coordinating, and what two errors does it prevent?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Smoothly trading clutch release for light gas prevents intersection stalls and screaming neutral revs.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: Where on the steering wheel rim should your two hands hold?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Balanced hands on opposite sides give instant two-way steering leverage if a pothole or gust tugs a tire.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: Which steering method does Arkansas's guide specify for sharp turns—and what habit must you skip?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Palming a slick steering rim with one open hand slips easily mid-corner when you need crisp control.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: How should you bring the steering wheel back to straight after rounding a turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Letting a spinning wheel whip freely through open fingers risks over-shooting into adjacent lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: How do posted speed signs and live road conditions work together to set safe speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Posted signs cap dry-day maximums while rain, glare, or congestion push your safe speed lower.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: Which dashboard gauge should you glance at regularly to prevent unintentional speeding?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Quiet highway cabins mask rising speed on gentle downhill grades until you check the dial.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: How does scanning well down the road keep your braking smooth?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Catching red brake lights a block ahead lets you ease off the gas gently instead of spiking brakes.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: What vehicle-control danger comes from stomping the brake pedal suddenly and hard?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Overwhelming tire grip in a panic stomp turns rolling steering tires into sliding hockey pucks.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: How does losing control during abrupt braking endanger drivers around you?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Surrounding drivers cannot predict which lane a sideways skidding car will sweep across next.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: What broad rule defines distracted driving in Arkansas's guide?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Distraction isn't limited to cell phones—any habit stealing mental, visual, or physical focus qualifies.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: Beyond phones, which everyday inside-the-car habits does the guide list as distractions?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Unwrapping burgers, reaching for spilled cups, or programming navigation mid-lane steals critical seconds.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: Why does safe driving demand one hundred percent of your attention?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Traffic shifts in split seconds, turning even brief side tasks into rear-end or lane-drift collisions.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: What specific part of driving focus does a visual distraction steal?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Reading a two-second notification banner leaves your car rolling blind past crosswalks and brake lights.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: What does a manual distraction remove from vehicle control?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Reaching into a bag or holding food leaves one—or zero—hands ready when wind gusts or blowouts hit.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: What does a cognitive distraction pull away from driving?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Daydreaming or arguing on speakerphone causes inattention blindness even while eyes stare straight ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: Why are handheld calls and texting considered the ultimate distraction threat?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Texting hijacks eyes, fingers, and brain simultaneously—leaving nobody truly piloting the vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: What cell-phone rule governs Arkansas drivers younger than eighteen?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Test writers target Bluetooth loopholes—under eighteen in Arkansas bans both handheld and hands-free outside emergencies.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: How does the guide treat hands-free phone use starting at age eighteen?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Legal permission at eighteen doesn't erase mental distraction—skipping calls altogether stays safest.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What responsibility does the guide give a passenger riding with a distracted driver?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Passengers share the exact same crash physics—offering to handle navigation or calling out texting saves lives.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: Which two phone habits does Arkansas's guide urge every driver to pledge against behind the wheel?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Putting your phone on Do Not Disturb before shifting out of park removes temptation completely.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How many deaths and injuries in two thousand twenty-two does the guide attribute to distracted driving?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Three thousand three hundred eight fatalities and two hundred ninety thousand injuries show how deadly quick glances turn.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, what landmark distance does the guide compare texting to driving blind across?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Five seconds of eyes-down texting at fifty-five miles per hour equals driving end-zone to end-zone blindfolded.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Which two age brackets hold larger shares of distracted drivers in fatal crashes according to the guide?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Both young smartphone-heavy cohorts and oldest senior cohorts show elevated distraction shares in fatal wrecks.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: Which three strategies combine in the national campaign against distracted driving?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Pairing tough statutes with visible patrol citations and education shifts everyday driver culture.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: What safety warning accompanies phone-use permission for drivers twenty-one and older?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Reaching twenty-one changes statutory phone rules, never human brain limits—talking while driving stays risky.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: How does the guide encourage drivers to carry anti-distraction safety into their social circle?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Talking openly with friends and family builds mutual expectations never to expect instant replies from drivers.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: How far down the street should you scan while driving in town?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Staring straight at the rear bumper right ahead blinds you to sudden mid-block hazards and forces panic braking.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: How far ahead should you scan on open highways and interstates?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Fast highway speeds eat up pavement rapidly, so spotting stalled traffic early buys smooth room to change lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: How many seconds ahead along your path should you plan your forward scan?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Planning a full fifteen-second visual lead lets you spot brake lights and merging cars well before trouble arrives.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: How can you check your forward viewing time while driving?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Counting toward a stationary roadside post confirms whether your eyes are actually scanning far enough ahead for your speed.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: Beyond standard cross streets, what everyday entrances count as road intersections?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Test takers forget private driveways and shopping-plaza aprons, even though cars dart out across traffic there constantly.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: What three-step visual scan should you make right before crossing an intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Traffic from the nearest lane reaches your door first, so rechecking approaching cars catches fast-closing surprises.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: Which three conflict sources must you scan before starting a right turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Drivers fixate left for a gap and miss an oncoming left-turner or a pedestrian stepping into the crosswalk.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: When may you turn right at a steady red light, and what forbids it?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Rolling past the line without stopping or missing a turn-prohibition sign triggers an automatic road-test failure.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What should you do if bushes or parked cars still block your view after stopping?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Pulling out blindly invites a side-impact crash, so inching ahead slowly after your legal stop opens sightlines safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: How should you keep track of vehicles behind you when traffic gets dense?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Frequent quick mirror sweeps reveal tailgaters and fast-closing cars before you ever touch the brake pedal.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: Which two visual checks are required before moving into another lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Relying on glass alone leaves a car-sized blind zone right beside your rear fender during a lane shift.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: At least how far ahead must you activate your turn signal before changing lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Flicking the lever mid-swerve gives surrounding drivers zero warning to hold speed or leave your gap open.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: What two things must you confirm about the next lane before sliding over?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Even an empty spot right beside you turns into a sideswipe if a faster car behind already started overtaking.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: Why must you glance over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Even well-aimed side glass leaves blind pockets that only a direct head turn toward your target lane clears.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Why must your over-the-shoulder head check stay quick and brief?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Staring backward too long leaves you blind if the car right in front suddenly slams on its brakes.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Which smaller road users require extra visual care when pulling out from a curb or driveway?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Narrow profiles blend behind parked cars and utility poles, making riders and pedestrians easy to overlook when pulling out.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does monitoring traffic behind you give you extra reaction time?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Catching a distracted speeder or bumper-hugger early lets you tap brakes gently or widen your front cushion.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: Which three driving moves require full lane-change mirror and shoulder checks?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Test questions group ramp merges and curbside pullouts with lane shifts because every lateral move crosses blind zones.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: Which two zones around your car must every lane-change check cover?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Checking only rear distance misses a quiet car cruising beside your door, while checking beside misses fast closers.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: Which specific parts of the area around your vehicle can mirrors fail to show completely?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Vehicles tucked off either rear quarter sit outside standard mirror angles until a quick shoulder glance exposes them.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: What two steps protect you from a rear-end hit right before slowing down?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Checking your mirror and easing into brake lights early warns trailing traffic before your speed drops sharply.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: What should you inspect before climbing into the driver's seat to back up?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Toddlers, pets, and bikes below trunk height stay completely invisible from the cabin once you sit down.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: How should you position yourself to see while backing instead of trusting mirrors alone?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Mirrors frame narrow slices of space, whereas turning to look directly through rear and side glass reveals cross-traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: How fast should you move when backing up, and why?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Front-wheel steering pivots the car awkwardly in reverse, so creeping at walking pace prevents wild swings into obstacles.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: What outside help should you use whenever available while backing?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: A trusted helper standing clear outside sees low curbs, tight corners, and approaching pedestrians your pillars hide.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: Which positions next to another vehicle should you avoid holding in traffic?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Cruising right beside or off another car's rear quarter leaves you invisible if that driver swerves for debris.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: What mistake must you avoid while overtaking another vehicle?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Hanging beside a vehicle mid-pass traps you right where the other driver cannot see you before changing lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.question_text: What lane position must you avoid around buses and tractor-trailers?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.teaching_text: Large buses and rigs carry massive side no-zones and need wide lateral room if wind or tire trouble hits.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: How does the Arkansas guide define a vehicle blind spot?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Pillars, headrests, cargo, and mirror limits block direct sight from the driver's seat, hiding nearby road users.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: How should you get out of another driver's blind spot when traffic paces together?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Gently easing off the gas or briskly finishing a legal pass restores clear visibility between both vehicles immediately.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: Why should you allow extra time when slowing for a private driveway or lot entrance?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Drivers expect stops at traffic lights, not unmarked driveways, so early signals and gradual braking prevent rear-end hits.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: What arm and torso position does the guide suggest for looking straight back while reversing?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Draping your right arm across the passenger seatback pivots your shoulders naturally for a wide rear-window view.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: What safety danger rises when vehicles share a road at wildly different speeds?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Drivers crawling far slower or racing far faster than the pack force constant sudden braking and lane swerves.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: How does matching safe legal traffic flow affect how often you need to pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Cruising smoothly with legal surrounding pace eliminates risky leapfrog lane swaps that barely save seconds anyway.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: What should you do if driving slowly causes a line of cars to stack up behind you?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Holding up a frustrated line tempts impatient drivers into blind two-lane passes right behind your bumper.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: How should you use a highway entrance ramp before blending into the travel lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Entering highway lanes way below flow speed forces fast trucks behind you to slam brakes or swerve.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Why must you avoid rolling to the very tip of an entrance ramp and stopping dead?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Drivers behind you glance left at highway traffic while accelerating, making a stopped bumper ahead an instant rear-end target.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: Where on an entrance ramp should you ease off if traffic has zero gap yet?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Easing speed near the start of the ramp preserves pavement ahead to punch up to speed once a gap opens.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: What last visual check must you make right before sliding from a ramp into traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Side mirrors leave a blind pocket right where highway right-lane cars cruise beside an incoming ramp.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: Where should you start slowing down when leaving a highway that has an exit ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Braking inside the fast through lane surprises high-speed traffic behind you instead of using the deceleration lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: How should you exit a fast two-lane highway that has no separate deceleration lane?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Without an exit lane to shelter you, early blinkers and gradual braking protect your rear bumper from fast followers.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: How should you handle your approach when you spot unusually slow traffic ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Closing distance shrinks shockingly fast against a crawling vehicle, so early lane shifts or coasting prevent panic stops.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: What speed change should you anticipate behind a heavy truck or weak car climbing a long hill?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Gravity drags loaded trucks down steep grades quickly, closing your following cushion much faster than on flat ground.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: What top speed and rear marker apply to farm tractors, horse buggies, and road graders?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Spotting that reflective rear slow-vehicle triangle warns you instantly that you are closing at highway-versus-tractor speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: Why must you drop speed through shopping districts, parking lots, and downtown blocks?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Drivers hunting spaces back out, brake suddenly, and cross paths from every angle with almost zero warning.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: Which four pinched or congested road features demand a drop in speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Concrete walls, bridge rails, toll lanes, and packed rush-hour queues strip away your side escape paths.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: How must you adjust near schools, playgrounds, and neighborhood streets?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Kids chase balls or ride bikes straight past parked cars without checking oncoming lanes first.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: Which two surprise hazards make weaving past car after car risky?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Each extra pass multiplies the odds a slower driver pulls left or an oncoming car crests a two-lane rise.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: What extra challenge hits heavy or slow vehicles pulling into traffic on an uphill grade?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Climbing gravity slows acceleration dramatically, so give uphill merging vehicles extra space or move over a lane.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: How does the clear road distance visible ahead set your safe top speed?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Outrunning your clear sightline guarantees a crash if a stalled car or fallen tree sits just beyond view.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: What maximum speed does the guide set when rain or fog cuts forward sight to two hundred feet or less?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: At higher speeds your total stopping distance exceeds two hundred feet, meaning you hit hidden hazards before halting.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: What must you do if blinding weather wipes out your view of the road ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Creeping blind in an active lane invites high-speed pileups, so get clear of pavement until skies open.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: How should you adjust speed when nearing a hill crest or blind curve?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Assuming empty pavement beyond a blind rise leaves zero room if a farm tractor or stopped queue sits there.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: What sudden hazards require extra room beside a line of parked cars?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: An unlatched driver door or a pedestrian stepping from between tall vans can fill a tight lane instantly.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: How do you run the guide's four-second sight-distance check on the road?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Timing your run to the farthest clear landmark tests whether fog, darkness, or curves have shrunk stopping sight.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: What action is required if you pass your landmark before finishing the four-second sight count?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Reaching that marker early proves you are outdriving your clear visibility and cannot stop inside what you see.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: Can an officer ticket you for driving too fast even when your speedometer matches the posted sign?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Speed signs apply to dry daylight pavement, so driving the max in ice or heavy fog violates basic speed law.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: What crucial advantage do you gain by keeping more space behind the vehicle ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Extra cushion turns a chain-reaction panic slam into a calm, controlled brake tap that protects everyone.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: How do you measure the guide's basic two-second following cushion behind a lead car?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Using a fixed shadow, sign, or overpass self-adjusts your following yardage automatically as speed rises or falls.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: What should you do if your bumper reaches the marker before your two-second count finishes?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Finishing under two seconds means you are tailgating inside reaction time, so drop back and verify again.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: Why must you stretch your following distance whenever pavement turns wet, snowy, or icy?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Reduced tire grip multiplies braking yards, making a dry-road two-second gap way too short to avoid rear-ending.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: How should you help a driver behind you who pulls out to overtake your vehicle?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Lifting slightly off the gas shortens their time in the oncoming lane and opens a safe landing spot ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: Why do motorcycles need extra following room on wet pavement, ice, loose gravel, or metal grates?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: With only two narrow contact patches, a rider can spill instantly on slick bridge grates or gravel without brake lights.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: Why should you drop farther back behind trucks, buses, vans, or trailers?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Tailgating a tall rear box hides your car from their side mirrors and blocks your own view of road hazards.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: How does pulling a trailer change your vehicle's stopping distance?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Extra trailer mass pushes forward hard under braking, demanding much wider following space ahead of your bumper.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: How must darkness, fog, or heavy rain change your following gap?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: When glare or mist hides brake lights two cars ahead, extra seconds keep you clear of sudden slowdowns.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: How should you manage space around police cruisers, ambulances, and fire engines?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Crews step out carrying gear and vehicles maneuver abruptly at scenes, so crowding emergency units puts lives at risk.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: Why must you keep extra space behind buses and hazmat tankers approaching train tracks?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: School buses, passenger buses, and placarded hazmat rigs must stop at crossings even when warning lights stay dark.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: Why should you leave extra bumper gap when stopped behind someone on an uphill slope?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: Manual transmissions and heavy loads often drift back a few feet as the driver moves from brake to gas.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: About how many total feet does the guide's example take to stop from forty miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Even moderate suburban speeds burn over a hundred twenty feet of reaction plus braking before tires stand still.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: About how many total feet does the guide's example require to stop from fifty-five miles per hour?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Adding just fifteen miles per hour past forty nearly doubles total stopping length to two hundred twenty-five feet.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Within what specific distance must you always be able to stop when driving at night?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Outrunning your low or high beams means any dark hazard ahead is already unavoidable the instant it appears.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: What kind of driving conditions are posted speed-limit signs built around?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Rain, ice, glare, or dense traffic shatter ideal assumptions and legally require slowing below the black-and-white number.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: To how many seconds does the guide stretch its basic two-second following rule in tough conditions?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Doubling from two seconds to four gives wet tires and dim visibility the extra stopping runway they demand.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: Which two habits help drivers behind you keep a safe cushion without surprises?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Predictable throttle control and early blinkers or brake taps stop accordion chain-reaction crashes behind your trunk.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: Where should you pull over to pick up or drop off riders safely?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: Stopping inside a live travel lane exposes swinging doors, distracted riders, and your rear bumper to moving cars.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.question_text: How should you handle traffic behind you right before backing into a parallel parking spot?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.teaching_text: Letting close trailing cars roll past first stops someone from nosing tightly behind your bumper as you shift reverse.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.question_text: How should you let faster vehicles pass when you are traveling slower than normal traffic?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.teaching_text: Using a paved turnout or wide safe shoulder clears faster traffic cleanly without risking half-lane straddling.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.question_text: What two calm moves does the guide give for shedding a driver tailgating you?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.teaching_text: Changing right frees the fast lane, and gently easing speed on two-lane stretches encourages a quick, low-risk pass.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.question_text: Why must you never slam or tap brakes sharply just to warn off a tailgater?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.teaching_text: A bumper-hugger already lacks reaction distance, so abrupt braking almost guarantees they plow straight into your trunk.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.question_text: How should you position your car relative to vehicles in neighboring lanes on a multilane road?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.teaching_text: Staggering into open pockets beside you leaves an instant escape lane if a tire blows or debris appears.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.question_text: Where inside your lane should you track instead of hugging the center line?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.teaching_text: Crowding the yellow center stripe slashes the margin between side mirrors when wide oncoming trucks sweep past.

sec12-card-sec12-F44.question_text: Why do parked cars along the curb deserve extra lateral clearance as you pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F44.teaching_text: Wide side room keeps a surprise door swing, hidden walker, or nose-out bumper outside your fender line.

sec12-card-sec12-F45.question_text: How should you steer when hazards box you in on both the left and right at once?
sec12-card-sec12-F45.teaching_text: Compromising between oncoming traffic and parked cars while giving extra inches to the deadlier threat minimizes crash severity.

sec12-card-sec12-F46.question_text: What should you do when approaching a bicyclist ahead at the exact moment an oncoming car nears?
sec12-card-sec12-F46.teaching_text: Squeezing three wide across two lanes invites a sideswipe or head-on crash, so wait behind the cyclist briefly.

sec12-card-sec12-F47.question_text: What must you do instead of squeezing inside the same lane alongside a pedestrian or cyclist?
sec12-card-sec12-F47.teaching_text: Sharing a single lane brushes dangerously close to handlebars or shoulders where one pothole wobble turns fatal.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: What should drivers on a multilane highway do when traffic is entering from an on-ramp?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Sliding left into an empty lane or adjusting pace opens a clean slot that keeps ramp traffic flowing safely.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: Which unprotected road users need generous side clearance and alertness for sudden moves?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Without steel cages around them, pedestrians, cyclists, and playful children need wide physical buffers for unexpected swerves.

sec12-card-sec12-F48.question_text: About how many seconds of open traffic gap does the guide recommend to merge, enter, or change lanes?
sec12-card-sec12-F48.teaching_text: A four-second opening lets you slot smoothly between two cars without forcing either driver to stomp brakes.

sec12-card-sec12-F49.question_text: How must you move across several highway lanes toward an exit or turn?
sec12-card-sec12-F49.teaching_text: Sweeping diagonally across three lanes blinds you to a car simultaneously merging into that middle lane from the far side.

sec12-card-sec12-F50.question_text: Why must you reject squeezing into a tight traffic gap that barely fits your car?
sec12-card-sec12-F50.teaching_text: Cutting tightly between bumpers wipes out stopping buffers instantly if the lead car taps brakes a second later.

sec12-card-sec12-F51.question_text: When is it safe to treat a highway median crossover as a halfway waiting zone?
sec12-card-sec12-F51.teaching_text: Stopping in a narrow median strip leaves your hood or trunk jutting straight into high-speed through lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F52.question_text: When must you hold back from starting a left turn even if oncoming lanes open up?
sec12-card-sec12-F52.teaching_text: Starting a turn into a crosswalk full of walkers or backed-up cars strands your side doors across oncoming lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F53.question_text: What must you do at a green traffic light when backed-up cars block the far side of the intersection?
sec12-card-sec12-F53.teaching_text: Rolling inside on green only to get trapped when lights change blocks cross-traffic and triggers a gridlock citation.

sec12-card-sec12-F54.question_text: Why should you wait before pulling out in front of an oncoming car whose turn signal is blinking?
sec12-card-sec12-F54.teaching_text: Drivers forget signals constantly or aim for a driveway past yours, so wait until the car visibly slows and turns.

sec12-card-sec12-F55.question_text: How many vehicles should you generally overtake per pass instead of stringing several together?
sec12-card-sec12-F55.teaching_text: Stringing multiple cars together hides gaps closing up front and leaves you stranded in the oncoming lane.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: How much front and rear cushion do you create by centering your car inside a four-second gap?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Landing dead center inside four seconds automatically gives both you and the driver behind a two-second buffer.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: Why is an oncoming motorcycle's flashing turn signal extra risky to trust?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Many motorcycles lack steering-wheel auto-cancel switches, so riders cruise straight for miles with an old blinker flashing.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: Which two everyday reasons explain why a blinking oncoming car still blasts straight past you?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Whether they signaled early for the next corner or never canceled an old turn, pulling out causes an angle crash.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.question_text: Which two actions must your chosen cross-traffic gap cover when turning onto a fast road?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.teaching_text: Clearing the corner alone is half the battle if fast oncoming traffic still slams your rear bumper while accelerating.

sec12-card-sec12-F56.question_text: What is the only right decision if you hesitate over whether time and space allow a pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F56.teaching_text: Head-on closing speed doubles highway pace, turning a half-second misjudgment into an unsurvivable two-lane collision.

sec12-card-sec12-F57.question_text: Within what distance of a hill or curve does the Arkansas guide forbid passing?
sec12-card-sec12-F57.teaching_text: An unseen car cresting a hill inside a third of a mile closes on your nose before you clear the truck.

sec12-card-sec12-F58.question_text: Which three junction types must you avoid passing near because cross-traffic can enter?
sec12-card-sec12-F58.teaching_text: Passing across intersections, rail tracks, or shopping-center aprons puts you broadside into turning or crossing vehicles.

sec12-card-sec12-F59.question_text: What roadside or lane conditions ahead should you scan for before starting a pass?
sec12-card-sec12-F59.teaching_text: A parked car, pothole, or cyclist up ahead may force the driver you are passing straight left into your door.

sec12-card-sec12-F60.question_text: What must be waiting ahead of the vehicle you plan to pass before you ever pull out?
sec12-card-sec12-F60.teaching_text: Pulling out alongside a tight bumper-to-bumper line traps you in oncoming lanes with nowhere to tuck back in.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.question_text: Roughly how many seconds and what opposing gap does a pass at fifty-five miles per hour require?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.teaching_text: Over ten seconds both you and an oncoming driver cover massive highway ground toward the exact same spot.

sec12-card-sec12-R15.question_text: Why is it so hard to judge the closing speed of a distant oncoming vehicle on a straight road?
sec12-card-sec12-R15.teaching_text: Far down a flat highway a tiny silhouette barely grows at first, hiding seventy-mile-per-hour speed until way too late.

sec12-card-sec12-R16.question_text: What deadly hazards can the vehicle you are overtaking hide from view near a crossing?
sec12-card-sec12-R16.teaching_text: A tall van or truck beside you acts like a moving wall, screening crossing pedestrians, cross-traffic, or approaching trains.

sec12-card-sec12-R17.question_text: What mirror cue confirms you have enough clearance to pull back right after a nighttime pass?
sec12-card-sec12-R17.teaching_text: Darkness distorts side-mirror depth, whereas seeing both beams in your center mirror proves you cleared their front bumper.

sec12-card-sec12-R18.question_text: What is the primary reserved purpose of the left lane on a multilane Arkansas highway?
sec12-card-sec12-R18.teaching_text: Camping in the left lane clogs highway flow and pushes impatient traffic into risky right-side weaving.

sec12-card-sec12-R19.question_text: When does road construction legally allow continuous travel in the left highway lane?
sec12-card-sec12-R19.teaching_text: Barrels and crews shutting every right-hand lane make the open left lane the sole legal through path.

sec12-card-sec12-R20.question_text: What pavement or surface condition lets you legally stay in the left highway lane?
sec12-card-sec12-R20.teaching_text: Flooded ruts, deep ice, or major debris in right lanes justify holding the clear left lane safely.

sec12-card-sec12-R21.question_text: Which upcoming ramp maneuver permits moving into and holding the left highway lane?
sec12-card-sec12-R21.teaching_text: Positioning left early avoids last-second multi-lane dives when your highway ramp peels off from the left.

sec12-card-sec12-R22.question_text: Which roadside users or surface obstacles can suddenly wipe out the lane space you planned to pass in?
sec12-card-sec12-R22.teaching_text: Scanning far ahead spots narrow bridge rails, cyclists, potholes, or ice patches before they pinch your passing lane shut.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: How does a tractor-trailer stopping distance compare with a passenger car traveling at the exact same speed?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Cutting tightly in front of heavy freight steals the extra braking margin required to prevent a rear-end crash.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: Roughly what total stopping distance does the Arkansas guide give for an average passenger car moving at fifty-five miles per hour?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Drivers consistently underestimate highway braking space, turning ordinary lane merges into sudden emergency slam-stops.

sec13-card-sec13-F03.question_text: How much stopping distance can a fully loaded tractor-trailer need when traveling at fifty-five miles per hour?
sec13-card-sec13-F03.teaching_text: Massive cargo momentum stretches highway braking well past a football field, leaving zero room for abrupt lane jumpers.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: When any vehicle turns a corner, how does the path of its rear wheels compare with its front wheels?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Longer trailers sweep sharply across inside lanes and curbs, crushing cars that squeeze into the corner gap.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: Why might a tractor-trailer swing toward the left before making a turn at an intersection?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Test-takers and impatient drivers mistake that wide setup swing for a lane change and get trapped curbside.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: What should you verify before trying to pass a large truck that begins shifting to the left?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Slipping down the open right side during a wide-turn setup puts your car directly beneath the swinging trailer.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: Why is it unsafe to expect a tractor-trailer to handle and maneuver like an oversized passenger car?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Assuming passenger-vehicle agility around commercial rigs causes drivers to misread wide turns, slow starts, and long stops.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Do a commercial driver's elevated seat and oversized mirrors get rid of serious blind spots around the rig?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Many motorists assume high seating grants total visibility, leading them to camp right inside hidden danger zones.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: Within how much space directly ahead of a tractor-trailer cab can a passenger car disappear from the driver's view?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Merging right across a tall hood hides your entire roof below the trucker's sightline during heavy traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: Where do side blind spots stretch along a tractor-trailer, and where are they especially severe?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Cruising beside the tractor doors leaves you invisible when the rig needs to swerve around highway debris.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: How far behind a tractor-trailer can the rear blind area extend according to the Arkansas guide?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Solid trailer doors block any center rearview mirror, hiding tailgating cars across an enormous stretch of pavement.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: How does hanging out beside or right behind a truck in its blind area affect the truck driver?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: When blown tires or stalled cars appear ahead, unseen vehicles alongside trap the rig or get sideswiped.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: What should you assume whenever you cannot see a truck driver's reflection in the rig's side mirror?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Light travels both ways in flat and convex glass, making that quick mirror glance an instant visibility test.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: What visibility advantage and disadvantage come together from sitting up inside a tall truck cab?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Elevated seating helps spot distant traffic backups early while leaving deep unseen pockets right around the bumper and doors.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: Which three basic vehicle maneuvers require more space for a large truck than for a passenger car?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Crowding commercial vehicles during merges, corners, or slowdowns ignores the physics of moving tens of thousands of pounds.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: What must you avoid doing with a truck's open front cushion when approaching an exit, turn, or lane closure?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Diving across a rig's nose for a last-second ramp forces emergency air-brake lockups that can trigger a jackknife.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: How should you handle a highway exit when a large truck is already traveling right ahead in that lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Tucking smoothly behind the trailer costs only seconds while racing past its bumper risks a high-speed clip.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: Which side should you use to overtake a tractor-trailer, and how should you complete the pass?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Driver-side sightlines are narrower than right-side blind zones, and brisk completion keeps you clear of tire blowouts.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: Why must you never follow closely behind a large truck in traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: A tall trailer hides brake lights ahead, leaving zero time to avoid an underride collision if traffic halts.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: Beyond sudden braking, what roadway hazard makes extra following clearance behind a high-clearance truck essential?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Heavy axles can straddle or kick up tire treads and timber that smash straight into a close follower's windshield.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: Why do drivers need extra caution when judging an approaching tractor-trailer's speed from down the road?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Large objects appear to close distance leisurely to the human eye, luring drivers into pulling out way too late.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: What does the open gap a truck driver leaves in front of the cab actually represent?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Treating a trucker's intentional braking buffer like an empty parking spot strips away everyone's crash protection.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: What specific problem do you create if you linger right alongside a truck during a pass?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Staying boxed against a trailer's flank removes the driver's only lateral escape path when hazards appear ahead.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: Which two critical factors can a motorist easily misjudge when watching a large truck approach an intersection?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Pulling across an intersection on a bad read leaves a heavy rig zero chance to shed highway momentum.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: How do a commercial truck's weight and handling responsiveness compare with a standard passenger car?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Physics prevents a multi-ton vehicle from swerving or shedding speed quickly when smaller cars make abrupt mistakes.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: In the national comparison cited by the Arkansas guide, what share of fatal multivehicle tractor-trailer crashes is attributed to the passenger-car side?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Exam writers highlight this figure to prove passenger motorists control most of the risk around commercial freight.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: Which three personal conditions form the foundation for safe driving in the Arkansas guide?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Skipping sleep, ignoring blurry eyesight, or driving impaired breaks down hazard response before the engine even starts.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: What three critical driving tasks depend directly on having clear sight?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Delayed visual recognition shrinks your stopping margin until ordinary traffic shifts become last-second panics.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: What is peripheral vision, and how does it help while you are driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Motion entering from cross streets or adjacent lanes registers in your outer visual field before you turn your head.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: Because peripheral vision lacks sharp focus, what two habits should supplement it?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Relying on blurry outer sight alone misses fast-closing motorcycles or cars tucked along your rear quarter.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: During which two high-stakes maneuvers is judging vehicle distance and speed especially crucial?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Misjudging closing rates on ramps or undivided highways puts your bumper directly into oncoming or fast-moving traffic.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: How should you adjust your driving habits if you struggle to see well after dark?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: Low contrast and oncoming glare hide pedestrians and curves long before poor night eyes can spot them.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: How often does the Arkansas guide recommend having an eye specialist test your vision, and why?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Gradual eyesight decline creeps up so slowly that drivers rarely realize road signs blurred until tested.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: What does Restriction B on an Arkansas driver license require whenever you are behind the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Permit exams frequently test this exact letter code because driving uncorrected turns a valid license into a violation.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: What practical eyewear precaution does the guide recommend keeping inside your vehicle?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Breaking or misplacing your everyday frames away from home could otherwise leave you stranded or driving half-blind.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: Why must you never wear sunglasses or tinted contact lenses while driving at night?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Filtering out scarce headlight illumination hides unlit hazards, dark clothing, and lane edges along rural roads.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: Which three specific traffic sounds can warn an alert driver of nearby danger?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Blasting cabin music drowns out early acoustic warnings from unseen emergency rigs or skidding brakes.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: How can a deaf or hard-of-hearing motorist safely make up for missed sound cues?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Frequent mirror sweeps and wide intersection scans catch flashing lights and closing traffic well ahead of time.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: What enforcement consequence can follow if you drive without corrective lenses required on your license?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Officers verify license restriction codes during routine stops, treating missing prescription eyewear as an immediate citation.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: In what physical state should you start a long highway drive rather than leaving tired?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Starting out exhausted guarantees highway hypnosis and delayed reactions well before your first fuel stop.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: What two scheduling habits help you complete a long road trip safely?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Unrealistic arrival targets push tired motorists to skip rest stops and speed through fading concentration.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: Which time window should you avoid when scheduling a long drive?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: Fighting circadian rhythm overnight triggers brief microsleeps even when a driver feels determined to push through.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: What is the right move when drowsiness hits behind the wheel instead of gambling on staying awake?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Rolling down windows or cranking the radio cannot stop a tired brain from nodding off mid-lane.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: How can minor ailments like a stiff neck, cough, or sore leg affect driving, and what should you do?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: Pain or coughing fits ruin shoulder checks and smooth pedal pressure right when traffic demands split-second control.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: Who should a motorist under treatment for a heart condition consult before getting behind the wheel?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Sudden dizziness or cardiac symptoms in moving traffic endanger everyone unless a physician confirms stability.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: How can intense feelings like worry, excitement, fear, anger, or sadness affect you on the road?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Mental preoccupation tunnels your attention inward so you miss red lights, brake lamps, and merging cars.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: What should you do before driving if you are heated with anger or overly worked up?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Bringing hot temper onto the street fuels aggressive tailgating, horn battles, and reckless lane cuts.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: How should a driver prone to impatience plan trips to avoid risky choices in traffic?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Running late turns minor red lights into temptations to speed, weave, or blow yellow signals.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Why does the Arkansas guide suggest eating lighter meals before setting out on a drive?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Post-meal sluggishness dulls highway focus and speeds up eyelid droop during monotonous stretches.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: What three restorative things do scheduled highway breaks let a driver do?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Getting blood moving outside the cabin shakes off stiff posture and resets visual alertness.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: What precaution does the guide give a person whose body is still adjusting to an insulin dose?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Unpredictable blood-sugar swings during dose changes can blur vision or cloud thinking mid-commute.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: Which specific insulin-related medical danger does the Arkansas guide warn must keep a driver off the road?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Sudden severe hypoglycemia can cause confusion or loss of consciousness while a vehicle is moving at speed.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: According to the Arkansas guide, how much alcohol concentration in the body is considered safe for driving?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: Test questions bait learners with legal thresholds, whereas impairment actually begins with the very first drink.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: Does years of driving experience protect a motorist from alcohol impairment compared with newer drivers?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: Seasoned habits cannot override chemically slowed brain signaling, while novices face an even steeper skill drop.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: Which essential driving ability is the very first one harmed after consuming alcohol?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: Exam writers love this trap because drivers lose realistic self-assessment long before their speech slurs.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: How does alcohol change your reaction speed, eyesight, and overall alertness?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Combining delayed braking feet with fuzzy focus turns routine intersection stops into rear-end crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: What happens to your decision-making and car-handling abilities as more alcohol builds up in your system?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Every added drink compounds poor risk choices with sloppy lane tracking and erratic pedal inputs.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: Which three attributes of other vehicles become harder to judge accurately under alcohol impairment?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: Impaired depth perception tricks motorists into turning right across fast oncoming headlights.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.question_text: What transportation plan should you set up before social drinking, and what if none is arranged?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.teaching_text: Locking in a sober ride ahead of time prevents impaired late-night rationalizations in the parking lot.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.question_text: Should you drive after drinking if you still feel steady and confident in your control?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.teaching_text: Because alcohol numbs self-criticism first, feeling totally fine is the classic symptom of impaired judgment.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.question_text: Do coffee, cold showers, brisk air, or exercise sober an impaired person up faster?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.teaching_text: Caffeine or cold water merely creates a wide-awake impaired driver whose blood alcohol stays unchanged.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.question_text: What does food in the stomach actually do to alcohol absorption, and does it stop intoxication?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.teaching_text: Meals delay how fast alcohol hits the blood, yet heavy drinking still pushes impairment into dangerous territory.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.question_text: What is the single thing that clears alcohol out of the human body?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.teaching_text: Liver metabolism works at a fixed biological pace that no folk remedy or willpower can speed up.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.question_text: What can happen to your driving privilege if you refuse a lawful alcohol test?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.teaching_text: Motorists wrongly think declining the machine dodges trouble, when refusal triggers its own license loss.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: Beyond crash danger, what legal and financial penalties can follow a drinking-and-driving violation?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: One impaired drive can trigger years of sky-high insurance rates, breath-lock hardware, and lost mobility.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: How does consumed alcohol travel through the body to disrupt safe driving?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Once absorbed into circulation, alcohol reaches neural centers governing steering precision and risk evaluation within minutes.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: By the moment a drinker consciously feels buzzed, what has already happened to their driving judgment?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Waiting until you feel tipsy to stop driving means critical decision errors are already underway.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: What is the difference between blood alcohol concentration and breath alcohol concentration?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: Enforcement statutes reference both sample types so roadside breathalyzers and lab draws carry clear legal meaning.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.question_text: Under what age is buying or consuming alcohol illegal in Arkansas?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.teaching_text: Zero-tolerance rules back up the age limit with strict driver-license consequences even outside a vehicle.

sec15-card-sec15-R12.question_text: What fine range, maximum jail exposure, and license suspension apply to a first alcohol-violation conviction in the Arkansas guide?
sec15-card-sec15-R12.teaching_text: Exam items test exact first-conviction numbers so new drivers see how costly even a single offense becomes.

sec15-card-sec15-R13.question_text: How do penalties change for drivers convicted of subsequent alcohol violations?
sec15-card-sec15-R13.teaching_text: Arkansas law ratchets punishments sharply upward on repeat offenses to pull chronic impaired drivers off public roads.

sec15-card-sec15-R15.question_text: What fine and driver-license penalty can strike an underage driver convicted of an alcohol violation in the guide?
sec15-card-sec15-R15.teaching_text: Losing driving privileges all the way to adulthood derails school, jobs, and independence from one bad night.

sec15-card-sec15-R16.question_text: How can an alcohol purchase or possession conviction affect driving privileges for someone under twenty-one?
sec15-card-sec15-R16.teaching_text: Teens often miss that getting caught buying or holding alcohol can suspend a license without ever touching a car.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.question_text: Can legal prescription or over-the-counter medicines make you unsafe to drive?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.teaching_text: Cold tablets, allergy pills, and pain prescriptions can dull reflexes just as severely as illicit substances.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.question_text: What two steps should you take before driving after starting any medication?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.teaching_text: Checking side effects ahead of time keeps unexpected dizziness or blurred focus from ambushing you mid-commute.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.question_text: Why must you never mix alcohol with prescription medicines or other drugs?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.teaching_text: Combined chemicals amplify sedation and coordination loss far beyond what either substance would trigger by itself.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.question_text: After a brief burst of wakefulness, what dangerous side effects can stimulant or diet pills trigger?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.teaching_text: Relying on pep pills for highway stamina backfires when jitters, tunnel vision, and sudden exhaustion hit mid-drive.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.question_text: Which four core driving abilities can other drugs impair in ways similar to alcohol?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.teaching_text: Whether impairment comes from a bottle or another drug, slowed eyes and bad choices cause identical crashes.

sec15-card-sec15-F40.question_text: What two major harms does the Arkansas guide link directly to illegal drug use?
sec15-card-sec15-F40.teaching_text: Unpredictable street potency destroys coordination behind the wheel while inflicting lasting damage on the body.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.question_text: What routine habit best lowers your odds of facing a sudden mechanical breakdown on the road?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.teaching_text: Catching worn pads, cracked belts, and aging tires in the driveway prevents panic failures at highway speed.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.question_text: In the brake-failure response described by the Arkansas guide, what should you try first with the brake pedal?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.teaching_text: Rapid strokes can rebuild enough hydraulic line pressure in a failing dual-circuit system to slow the car.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.question_text: If pumping the foot pedal fails to restore braking, how should you use the parking brake?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.teaching_text: Yanking the cable hard locks rear tires instantly and spins the car sideways out of control.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.question_text: What must you stay ready to do while applying the parking brake during an emergency stop?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.teaching_text: Keeping the release button or lever ready lets rear tires regain rolling grip before the tail swings around.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.question_text: If both pedal pumping and gradual parking-brake pressure fail to stop you, what should you do next?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.teaching_text: Stepping down through lower gears uses engine compression to scrub momentum while you steer onto safe shoulder ground.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.question_text: Once you bring a vehicle with failed brakes to a halt, may you keep driving it carefully?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.teaching_text: Limping home without reliable stopping power turns the very next downhill or red light into a wreck.
